commits.pr_title: [Doc] Kimi-K3: move the GB300 AgentX presets to the Oct 26 points with KV-balanced decode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Update the two GB300 Kimi-K3 AgentX disaggregated presets in `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml` to the lanes qualified in [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4638](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4638) (head `bc4d49f5`, sweep run [40830592414](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40830592414), attempt 1): `kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg` (preset `gb300_agentx_pd`) and `kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dep16-disagg` (preset `gb300_agentx_pd_dep16`). Both lanes now run image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505` (vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev229+g3966924d5` in the run logs) with Dynamo `a0de541ea8c861d5ac01d15953ca529bea68637b`, and their throughput points run decode attention on `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`. Each preset now has one `points.` per measured operating point, and the worker commands, environment block and Mooncake connector move out of the runbooks into structured fields. No open PR updates these lanes or their points; #64586 (drop dead envs from Kimi-K3) and #64617 (a B300 preset) edit the same file, so whichever merges second needs a rebase. ## Claims **`gb300_agentx_pd` (AgentX xPyD, default on GB300 `pd_cluster`, as before):** - `source` is #4638 at `bc4d49f5df307680be5a1567e01b838b83b31b62`. The image is pinned by digest (`@sha256:f255c4fa…`), and the Dynamo commit is unchanged. - There are 10 points with stable ids, one per measured point, matching the lane's search space: - **Specialized decode** (`TOKENSPEED_MLA`, `latency_specialized`, `--max-num-seqs 12`): `1p3d_c16`, `1p2d_c24` (the default point, as the preset rendered before) and `1p2d_c32`. - **Regular decode** (`KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`): `2p4d_c112`, `2p4d_c128`, `2p3d_c128`, `2p3d_c152`, `3p4d_c240`, `3p3d_c240` and `3p3d_c264`. - The 1P2D c48/c64 and 2P3D c240 points are no longer run, so they are dropped. - Regular points use these settings: - **Both roles:** BF16 SSM state and FlashInfer autotune on. - **Decode:** `--attention-backend KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`, with the DSpark draft's `attention_backend` on the same backend; `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv: 8` in `--attention-config`; `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512` and `--use-replayssm`; vLLM's default CUDA graph mode. - **Prefill:** stays on `TOKENSPEED_MLA` for target and draft. - Specialized points keep the earlier profile on both roles: FP32 SSM state, `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1` and autotune off. - Both roles move the NIXL + Mooncake store `MultiConnector` from the runbook into structured fields. It comes from `select.kv_offload: kv_store_distributed_mooncake`, with `json_args` for the lane's connector options: recompute on failed loads, `kv_buffer_device: cuda`, `enforce_handshake_compat: false`, `enable_cross_layers_blocks: false` and `enable_offload: false`. - The decode role drops the DEP-only `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` and `--no-enable-prefix-caching` with `remove_args`, replacing the earlier undo flags. - Environment additions on both roles, as the lane sets them: `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=0` on decode too, `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=120` and `ETCD_LEASE_TTL=600`. - Prefill KV events (`--kv-events-config`) are removed, because the lane no longer publishes them. **`gb300_agentx_pd_dep16` (AgentX 3P1D DEP16, opt-in):** - `source` is #4638 at the same commit, and the image is the same digest-pinned image. - The decode role runs target and draft attention on `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`. Prefill stays on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`. - There are three points, `c256`, `c288` and `c336` (default). The lane runs one configuration at all three client counts. - The KV connector comes from the same `select` + `json_args`. The decode role also sets the store child to `kv_consumer` with `enable_lookup: false`. - Prefill KV events are removed. **Runbooks** keep the evidence and processes the builder does not render: - the worker-count table; - multi-tray launch notes; - the specialized-decode and KV-balanced notes; - the Dynamo parser flags; - the etcd/NATS/Mooncake master commands and the lane's store configuration (160GB per rank, 60 s lease); - the frontend (`least-loaded`, session affinity). The duplicated Workers/Environment command blocks are removed. `meta.date_updated` is set to 2026-10-29. ## Validation - `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir /recipes` passes (vllm-project/recipes @ `2ac6bc4`): 220 recipes, JSON API built. - I built the full JSON API before and after the change. Only Kimi-K3 family files change: - `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.json` and its promoted variants `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-NVFP4`, `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-FP8-BLOCK` and `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8` (only `presets` and `meta.date_updated` change); - `presets/gb300_agentx_pd.json` and `presets/gb300_agentx_pd_dep16.json`; - the three `hw/gb300/strategies/pd_cluster.json` files. No `strategy_overrides`, hardware or variant field changes, so the Baseline (non-preset) commands are unchanged on every GPU and strategy. The default GB300 `pd_cluster` rendering (default preset, point `1p2d_c24`) changes only in: - the digest-pinned image; - the Mooncake `MultiConnector` with `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` and `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, which the builder's Mooncake option adds; - the dropped DEP undo flags; - the env additions above. - **Against the source:** every one of the 13 rendered points matches the lane's effective arguments and environment on both roles at the PR head. The script merges `disagg-variants.yaml` / `disagg-tp8-dep16.yaml` base roles with each point's override and checks against the master config's search space: concurrency, prefill and decode worker counts, two trays per TP8 worker and four per DEP16 worker, and the image. The only flags the builder adds are restatements of the lane's effective values: - `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`; - `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` on the xPyD pools; - `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` on the DEP16 decode, which the lane's per-node DP launch also adds; - `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` next to `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` on the specialized prefill. - **Against the logs:** the rendered `2p4d_c112` and `c256` prefill and decode commands and environment match the launch commands logged in run 40830592414 (2P4D c112 and 3P1D c256 eval jobs), apart from placement, parser and InferenceX plumbing (listed below). The worker logs show: - decode `Using AttentionBackendEnum.KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA backend` (32x per job) and prefill on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`; - `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` on both xPyD roles; - the prefill CUDA graph mode `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. - **Accuracy**, from the sweep's eval jobs with block verification: Kimi tool-call schema `em_strict` 0.985-0.998 (n=408) at every point, and GSM8K `em_strict` 0.966-0.972 (n=1319) where run. ## Details **Schema limitations:** - **Worker counts:** the builder renders one prefill and one decode worker per pool, so the xPyD counts (for example 2P4D) cannot be expressed. Each point's label, description and the runbook table give them. Role `nodes` stays at two trays per TP8 worker, because a larger `nodes` would render one wider TP group instead of more workers. - **Mooncake master and store sizing:** the master options and store sizing are not preset fields. The builder's Mooncake option shows its own defaults (100GB segment, 30 s lease), so the runbook gives the lane's values. - **Router and session affinity:** the Dynamo frontend's router mode and session affinity are not builder fields. **`gb300_low_latency` is unchanged.** The #4638 aggregated `dcp8-agg` c1 point is an image-only bump, and its serving flags already match that preset's `tp16` point, apart from the image and the synthetic acceptance. A point can pin its own `image`, but `source` (href/key/revision) exists only on the preset, and that preset cites vllm-project/recipes#1134 with the rolling `nightly` image for both its points. Citing the InferenceX key would mean re-sourcing or splitting that preset, so I left it. **Excluded as InferenceX-only, placement or no-op:** - **Benchmark controls:** concurrency lists, synthetic acceptance (`rejection_sample_method: synthetic`, `synthetic_acceptance_length` on throughput runs; the presets keep block verification), AIPerf/trace-replay settings, `dram-utilization` and Tachometer (disabled in #4638). - **Harness plumbing:** `--served-model-name` and the local `/model` path, `--device-ids`, `--dump-config-to`, `--request-plane tcp` (the builder sets `DYN_REQUEST_PLANE=tcp`), Slurm/container/health-check settings, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, `TILELANG_CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES`, `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM`, `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN`, the per-host Mooncake/NIXL/OTEL addresses, and `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST` (a site value; the runbook says to set it). - **Eval-only parsers:** `--dyn-tool-call-parser`, `--dyn-reasoning-parser` and `--dyn-enable-structural-tag`, which the runbook documents. - **No-op envs:** `VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT` and `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`. The lane sets them, but vLLM at the pinned commit `3966924d` reads neither (`git grep` finds no reference under `vllm/`), and `prefix_cache_retention_interval` already defaults to 0 (`vllm/config/cache.py`). #64586 removes them from the other Kimi-K3 presets. **Known renderer behaviour:** like the other presets that tune a composed connector by name, the `json_args` on `--kv-transfer-config` assume the Mooncake store selected by the preset. If a user turns that KV offload option off while the preset is active, the renderer raises an error for the missing `MooncakeStoreConnector` child. ### Generated preset JSON, before and after Condensed: the default point in full (`docker_*`/`command` fields and per-host env omitted), then each other point's differences from it.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO: hybrid READ for several attention groups and shared-group speculative methods
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) cannot run MoRIIO hybrid READ P/D on `main`. It has two transferable attention groups (MLA + indexer, and the kpool tail ring, a `CircularBufferSpec`), KDA groups, and MTP. `main` allows one attention group and DSpark only. With the packed `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` layout, `main` also classifies KDA groups as attention and silently skips recurrent-state transfer.

Changes (connector-only: `moriio_connector.py`, tests, one docs line):

- Hybrid READ payload is `[*attn_groups, *mamba_groups]`, byte-identical to `main` with one attention group.
- `_align_read_blocks` runs per attention group. Non-prefix-cacheable groups are read even on a full local hit.
- Each hybrid layer is routed to its own payload group. READ destinations of all attention groups are excluded from KV zeroing.
- A group is Mamba when every layer spec it covers is a `MambaSpec`.
- READ: the DSpark-only check is replaced by "the drafter shares the target's attention groups" (MTP, DSpark). Hybrid WRITE (#60544) is unchanged, including its DSpark check.
- `CircularBufferSpec` is accepted only for hybrid READ. Non-hybrid and hybrid WRITE still fail closed (`NotImplementedError` at init).
- Usage guide: drop the single-attention-group requirement.

Scope:

- Non-hybrid models do not reach the changed code (all scheduler changes are under `_has_mamba`).
- Single-attention-group hybrid READ is covered by byte-identity unit tests only.
- Drafters with a separate attention group are out of scope.

Requires #58585 (per-layer `block_len`), merged. The branch includes `main` with #60544 (hybrid WRITE).

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
```

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, MI300X.

E2E: GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, 1P/1D, MoRIIO READ, MTP 1, EP8 per leg, KV block 8, MI300X; `main` 19b0efce30 + this PR only.

## Test Result

### Unit

- On the merge with `main` a7407ab445 (incl. #62473): all `test_moriio_*.py` 878 passed, 0 failed (872 on `main`).
- Two `main` tests are intentionally replaced: the multiple-attention-group rejection and the READ case of the non-DSpark rejection.
- New tests: GLM-5.3-Flash grouping with MTP, payload pairing (partial/full hit), per-layer routing, single-group byte-identity, no-attention-group gate, `CircularBufferSpec` rejection (non-hybrid, hybrid WRITE), WRITE non-DSpark rejection. The non-hybrid gate test fails on the previous head.

The guard's contract is which branch runs, so the test now checks that directly, regardless of what else is profiling the process.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Skip AITER tuned GEMM when M*N >= 2^31 on gfx950
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip AITER's tuned GEMM (`tgemm.mm`) on gfx950 when M·N ≥ 2^31 (Also skip AITER tuned GEMM when A or B spans >= 4 GiB) and fall back to `F.linear` (hipBLASLt). This works around an int32 output-offset overflow in AITER's gfx950 FlyDSL A16W16 kernel (fix pending in ROCm/aiter#6853). Since AITER v0.1.26, that overflow crashes `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` at startup with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.

## Claims

- Fixes the `Memory access fault ... Write access to a read-only page` crash during the encoder-cache profile run of MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on MI355X (TP4) with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.
- No performance cost: only GEMMs with ≥ 2^31 output elements are rerouted, and hipBLASLt matches the FlyDSL kernel's throughput at those sizes. Normal LLM prefill/decode GEMMs never reach this size.

## Validation

Environment: MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, AITER 0.1.26.

**Kernel-level repro** (`tgemm.mm` vs `F.linear`, N=6144, K=1280, bf16, with bias; this matches the tuned `minimax_m3_mxfp4_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` rows):

| M | M·N vs 2^31 | `tgemm.mm` (AITER) | `F.linear` (hipBLASLt) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 340,000 | below | 1221 TFLOP/s | 1206 TFLOP/s |
| 360,000 | above | Memory access fault | n/a |
| 768,000 | above | Memory access fault | 1229 TFLOP/s |

**End-to-end** with this patch:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 -tp 4 --trust-remote-code --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --moe-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 
```

Before: crashes at startup with the memory access fault. After: startup completes (178 GiB KV cache on TP0), and three chat requests with a 2016×2016 image return 200 with no faults. Confirmed there is no accuracy change.

No unit test is added: reproducing the bug needs gfx950 hardware plus AITER's model-specific tuned CSV, and a mocked test would only restate the condition.

## Details

**Root cause.** With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, each rank runs the ViT unsharded, so the profile run issues an M=768000, N=6144, K=1280 GEMM with bias. In AITER v0.1.26, `getPaddedM` maps it to the `8192,6144,1280` FlyDSL row in `minimax_m3_mxfp4_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv`. That kernel computes `global_row * n + global_col` in int32, which wraps once M·N ≥ 2^31 and writes out of bounds. In TP mode N is sharded 4 ways, so M·N stays under the limit.

**Why route around it here.** `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` is the only vLLM call site of `tgemm.mm`. The guard is limited to gfx950 and to the exact overflow condition, so all other shapes keep AITER's tuned dispatch. Skipping FlyDSL for this call also avoids the FlyDSL 0.4.0 `from_dlpack` leak described in ROCm/aiter#6853, which pinned about 10.6 GiB after the ViT profile run.

The guard can be removed once vLLM's minimum AITER includes ROCm/aiter#6853.

## Overview With `--monokernel` on gfx950 (MI355X), DeepSeek-V4.1 decode batches of up to 32 rows now build their SWA metadata with `swa_decode_meta`'s single Triton launch (#60731). Before, they took vLLM's 8 launches per SWA group. #60731 enabled the kernel only on gfx942, but the kernel has no arch-specific code. This PR converges with #63994: it takes #63994's gate, `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` (`on_gfx942() or on_gfx950()`), and adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step and the GPU validation below. ## Claims - **49 fewer launches per decode step at c1: 114 to 65.** That is 7 SWA groups (4 target, 3 DSpark draft), each going from 8 launches to 1. Counted in a torch-profiler trace of each arm. - **Decode step (ITL p50): c1 -100 us (-1.75%), c2 -80 us (-1.16%).** - Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X TP4, `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6 (synthetic AL 3.87, AV off), 32k in / 1k out, on `main` nightly 5d35ce3934. - Runs: 2 rounds with the arms' GPU halves swapped. The per-round deltas are -1.85% and -1.66% at c1, and -1.70% and -0.61% at c2. - **Same metadata, same accuracy.** - On MI355X, the kernel test matches vLLM's ops. - With AV off, GSM8K matches base at 4 parallel requests, where every decode-only step takes the new path (6 runs per arm), and at 8 parallel (10 runs per arm). - Acceptance length (AL) on first passes and on passes with a per-request `cache_salt` is 3.577 in both arms. - With AV on (1 server per arm), GSM8K and AL match as well. - **Unchanged:** gfx942, runs without `--monokernel`, other arches, and prefill, mixed or >32-row batches. The gate test covers arch x flag; the row and prefill guards are #60731's and untouched. There is no new flag. ## Validation **Tests (MI355X, gfx950)** | Test | This PR | Before (PR base) | |---|---|---| | `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py`: kernel vs vLLM's ops, 300 random batches per case | `-k swa_decode_meta`: 2 passed; whole file: 3 passed | (kernel unchanged) | | `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`, with the new gate test (arch x `--monokernel`) | 82 passed | 81 passed, 1 failed: `[gfx950-True]` `assert [] == [False]` | | Extra, not in the PR: the kernel test with the target's 7 rows per request (k=6), the k=6 draft block, and 4 seeds x 500 batches | 8 passed: 4,000 batches; target rows 1-4 and 7/14/21/28, draft rows 6/12/18/24 at width 192 | | - **CI:** - The kernel test (`-k swa_decode_meta`) is added to `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics`. Per-server means: -0.006, below the 0.0077 binomial SE of a single run. | | Mono forced off, so the aiter attention reads the kernel's ragged views. 4 parallel, 2 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9132 | 0.9143 | +0.0011 | | Mono forced off, 8 parallel (mostly vLLM's views). 4 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9166 | 0.9177 | +0.0011 | | AV on, 8 parallel: 2 runs per arm, 1 server each | 0.9143 | 0.9166 | +0.0023 | | AV on, 4 parallel: 1 run per arm | 0.9227 | 0.9158 | -0.0068 (per-run sd is about 0.005) | | AL with AV off, on a first pass (only the shared 8-shot prefix cached) or with a per-request `cache_salt` (nothing cached). 8 runs per arm: 6 at 8 parallel, 2 at 4 parallel. | 3.577 | 3.577 | 0 | | AL with AV on, first pass | 3.373 | 3.383 | +0.010 | - **Run-to-run variation:** - Any two AV-off runs with mono on, at the same parallelism, on the same server or not, differ on 53-88 of the 1319 questions (53-92 including the mono-off runs). - Greedy decode on this stack is not run-to-run deterministic on either arm. The first token can differ even with a fresh `cache_salt`, so a text-identity check was not possible. - **The mono-off rows:** - With `--monokernel`, mono consumes only the dense indices and lengths. - The 4-parallel mono-off row is therefore the end-to-end check of the ragged indices, `indptr` and `is_valid_token`. **Sync check.** One TP4 server per arm ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, which polices the worker's `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` after warmup. Each served c1 and c2 (8 requests each, 512 out), 300 GSM8K questions at 4 parallel requests, and 4 greedy probes. Neither arm reported a sync, logged an error or failed a request.

c2: --max-concurrency 2 --seed 102 # GSM8K: sglang few_shot_gsm8k prompt and scoring, 8 shots, 1319 questions, temperature 0, max 512 tokens, # 8 or 4 parallel requests. # AL = 1 + delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total) / delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total) # Uncached passes: a unique "cache_salt" per request. # Tests on MI355X pytest tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py -k swa_decode_meta pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # Fail-before: keep the new test, restore the pre-PR vllm files, re-run. git checkout $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/__init__.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/swa_decode_meta.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # 81 passed, 1 failed ([gfx950-True]) ```
## Details **Change.** `ops.swa_decode_meta_enabled()`, the gate from #63994, returns true with `--monokernel` on ROCm when `on_gfx942()` or `on_gfx950()` holds. Only `swa_decode_meta.build` uses it. The other gfx942 helpers keep `ops.enabled()`. On gfx942 the two gates agree. **Limits.** - The kernel takes at most 32 rows; gfx950 mono takes up to 48. - With AV off at k=6, steps with 5 or more requests keep vLLM's build: the target at 35 or more rows, and the draft, which is padded to the 36-row graph. gfx942 behaves the same. - With AV on, the cutoff is 32 rows, not a request count. - AV-on `--monokernel` deployments now take this path. The AV-on round served without errors and matched base on accuracy and AL. **Related PRs.** - **#63994** (cpersson-amd) made the same change, and the two are converged here. This PR takes #63994's `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` gate, with Carl Persson as co-author of that commit. It adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step (#63994 used the optional `test-amd.yaml` step) and the GPU validation. #63994 can be closed. - **#58352:** it does not conflict textually, but the gains overlap. If it lands first, about 20 of the 49 launches remain (inferred, not measured). - **#61311** touches 4 of this PR's 5 files: `models_basic.yaml`, `ops/__init__.py`, `rocm.py` and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. - It renames `KernelConfig.monokernel` and `record_monokernel` to `specialized_decode`, and replaces `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` with `test_dsv41_specialized_decode.py`. - Whichever lands second rebases: rename `_monokernel` in `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` and move the gate test. - **#63486 (draft)** moves the DSv4.1 mono CI and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. If it lands first, I drop the `models_basic.yaml` hunk and move the gate test. - **#63891 (draft)** runs fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with `--monokernel`. It adds its own `mi3xx_enabled()` on `on_mi3xx()`, and the same review applies to it. Both PRs touch the same `models_basic.yaml` step and the `ops/__init__.py` docstring; the second to land merges those hunks.
Why the metadata is the same, and who reads it - **What the kernel writes.** `_decode_swa_meta_kernel` is integer Triton with no arch intrinsics. - For rows `[0, n)` it writes `is_valid_token` and the dense window indices and lengths. It sets the lengths from row `n` to the end of the buffer to 0. It writes `indptr[:n+1]` and the ragged indices up to `indptr[n]`. - These are the same values that `torch.ge`, the length fill, `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` (or `ComputeDSparkNoncausalSWAIndicesKernel` for the draft block), `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` and `_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers` produce. - `build()` returns views of the same persistent buffers, with the same lengths: ragged `[:max(n*width, 1)]` and `indptr[:n+1]`. - **Who reads it.** - **Mono:** with `--monokernel`, every target and DSpark-draft layer runs mono on decode-only steps of 48 rows or fewer that replay a FULL graph or run eagerly. Mono reads only the dense indices and lengths, `slot_mapping` and `token_to_req`. - **aiter sparse MLA:** on steps that mono declines, such as PIECEWISE steps, it (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA`) reads the ragged indices between `indptr[t]` and `indptr[t+1]`. It sizes its splits from the ragged view's `numel()`, which is `n*width` on both paths. - **Top-k build:** it reads `is_valid_token` on compressed layers. - Draft and target builders do not share buffers. - **The only bytes that differ** are the ragged entries past `indptr[n]`. vLLM's build copies them from a `torch.empty` tensor; the kernel leaves the previous contents. No reader reads past `indptr`. - **#60154** is on `main` but not in the measured image. It fuses inverse RoPE and the MXFP8 quant into the aiter sparse-MLA output, and does not change the index views that call reads. So this argument holds on current `main`.
An AL caveat for anyone reproducing (affects main, not this PR) On 4 of the 10 AV-off servers, AL fell from about 3.58 to 3.42-3.45 on GSM8K passes that repeated the same prompts. Those passes had about 96% prefix-cache hits, against about 89% on a first pass. The 4 servers were 2 base and 2 PR; one of the PR servers had mono forced off. - The two dropped servers that ran later passes stayed low. - On the one dropped server that also ran passes with a per-request `cache_salt`, those passes stayed at 3.58. - Accuracy did not move. - With AV on, the PR server's repeat pass also fell (3.383 to 3.279); base's did not (3.373 to 3.364). Compare AL on first or salted passes only. I will look into the drop separately.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-request draft retention for structured output under PP
commits.pr_body:
Co-authors: @michael-gpu, @tomasruizt 
cc @ArcheyChen 

## Overview

Revert https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442, which introduces a performance regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs, and re-fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54437 by addressing the root cause in `DraftTokensHandler`.

Rework of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61348, rebased, with remaining comments addressed, pre-commit fixed, and simplified implementation + tests.

## Claims

#54442 patched the issue in #54437 by masking out the draft tokens after a handoff race in `DraftTokensHandler`. This fixes #61348 but effectively shortens the draft sequence, causing an acceptance-length (and performance) regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs.

This PR addresses the `DraftTokensHandler` handoff race directly, fixing the original issue #54437 while maintaining acceptance length.

This PR also adds an E2E repro for #54437 and acceptance length regression.

## Validation

Correctness:

E2E repro in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py`, serves `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` + PP=2 and sends it a mix of constrained and unconstrained requests.

```
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py
```

On main, fails on `_assert_specdec_metrics`, showing a regression in acceptance rate and acceptance length
```
FAILED tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py::test_specdec_pp_structured_output[pp2-tp1] - AssertionError: (0.056471083070452156, 0.08341)
```

After revert #54442, fails on `_assert_outputs_are_structured`, showing unconstrained sampling reported by #54437
```
FAILED tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py::test_specdec_pp_structured_output[pp2-tp1] - AssertionError: ["blue", "
```

This branch
```
1 passed, 3 warning
```

More tests
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output

571 passed, 2 xfailed, 58 warnings

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_draft_tokens_handler.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model

140 passed, 3 skipped, 19 warnings
```

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e15dc602fbfd11e2b64c2d41527a1a72

`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark` + 8 draft tokens + async scheduling + structured outputs.
Ran on H100 80GB.

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ... --pipeline-parallel-size ... --num-repeats 10
```

Results report throughput in tokens/s.
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c96: low vs high concurrency
- 95% confidence intervals in brackets

No regression on PP=1

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 673.6 [668.3, 678.9] | 675.7 [666.5, 684.9] | +0.32%
broad / c96 | 9,835.7 [9,749.2, 9,922.2] | 9,785.8 [9,690.9, 9,880.7] | −0.51%
tight / c1 | 1,057.8 [1,047.7, 1,067.9] | 1,062.4 [1,051.7, 1,073.1] | +0.43%
tight / c96 | 18,582.1 [18,469.9, 18,694.3] | 18,565.3 [18,389.4, 18,741.2] | −0.09%

</body></html>

Recover performance regression on PP=2

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 661.45 [660.82, 662.08] | 662.79 [662.39, 663.19] | +0.20%
broad / c96 | 3,951.12 [3,822.93, 4,079.30] | 12,038.09 [11,768.25, 12,307.93] | +204.68%
tight / c1 | 1,021.45 [1,020.70, 1,022.19] | 1,024.63 [1,023.00, 1,026.26] | +0.31%
tight / c96 | 3,865.53 [3,771.94, 3,959.13] | 21,029.32 [20,574.89, 21,483.75] | +444.02%

</body></html>

## Details

### Background

`DraftTokensHandler` allows workers to asynchronously send draft tokens back to the scheduler / structured output manager for processing.

With async scheduling, it works roughly like:
```
Scheduler-side                          Worker-side
--------------------------------------------------
schedule step N
sample step N
                                        execute step N
schedule step N+1
wait for step N
                                        sample step N
                                        DraftTokensHandler.set_draft_tokens
                                        execute step N+1
DraftTokensHandler.get_draft_tokens
generate sampling bitmasks
sample step N+1
                                        sample step N+1
...
```

On main, `DraftTokensHandler` holds the latest batch set by the worker. This works fine for PP=1, but when PP>=2, this can occur:
```
Scheduler-side          Worker-side
----------------------------------
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch A)
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch B)
get_draft_tokens
```

Micro-batch B replaces micro-batch A in the handler. Scheduler-side cannot recover A's drafts and generates incorrect grammar bitmasks, leading to #54437.

#54442 fixes this by effectively truncating the worker-side draft sequence, reducing acceptance length.

This PR fixes this by making `DraftTokensHandler` track draft tokens by request ID. So micro-batch B cannot override micro-batch A.

Final notes:
- Suggest reviewing commits independently
  - `e3595db629d88881e74eafc357e471924b4d9c1f`: revert #54442, could be a separate PR
  - `c67afdec130ca06c6beb5e286a5b83b91fdae3a2`: track draft tokens by request ID.
  - `bb3694db86066ea2d272051b0495bad3ae09d026`: E2E repro
- Alternative #61348 includes adding a debug flag to catch the handoff race, this is not included in this PR in favor of the E2E repro.

commits.pr_title: [EPD] Metadata-only image and video inputs for GLM-5.3-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash can now take metadata-only image and video inputs in Python EPD, the same out-of-band placeholder path as Qwen-VL (#50390) and audio models (#57887). The encoder publishes `image_grid_thw`, and for video `video_grid_thw` plus one timestamp per temporal patch. The consumer rebuilds placeholders from those fields and receives embeddings through the EC connector.

No open PR covers this. #61418 is routing-metadata adapters, not EPD media metadata.

## Claims

- An EC consumer no longer reruns GLM-5.3-Flash vision preprocessing when the encoder published the placeholder metadata.
- On a cold 1E+1PD pair this is about 1.14× request throughput and 0.86× TTFT versus forwarding the raw image. The same ratio holds after each arm has warmed its own CUDA graphs.
- On 32 greedy image requests and 16 greedy video requests, prompt token counts and answer text matched the raw-media path on every request. Image and video throughput are separate tables. The image ratio above is not a video result.

## Validation

Not a duplicate of an open PR (search above).

AI assistance was used. The submitting human should review the diff.

Parser contract on the same H200 pod, against the installed tree with this patch (`pytest` 9.1.1, `torchvision` 0.28.0):

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/models/glm5next/test_epd_metadata.py
```

4 passed in 15.54s.

End-to-end on 8× H200, `zai-org` checkpoint `/models/GLM-5.3-Flash` (bf16/fp8), vLLM 0.32.0 plus this patch. The PD worker loads the full checkpoint, 76.5 GiB per TP=4 rank, so the PD side is TP=4 on GPU 4–7. The encoder is a dedicated `ec_producer` and runs encoder-only. In the throughput runs it was also started at TP=4 on GPU 0–3, and each encoder worker loaded 1.17 GiB; a later startup of this patch with `--tensor-parallel-size 1` loaded 1.93 GiB and used 4579 MiB on one GPU. Encoder TP=4 was not required for the vision tower. `ECExampleConnector` over local disk was used because `ECMooncakeConnector` producers require `tensor_parallel_size=1`, and the producer was originally launched with the full-model command. That check does not rule out Mooncake for an encoder-only producer. The tables below were measured with encoder TP=4 and `ECExampleConnector`. Max model len 8192, prefix caching left on for the PD instance, CUDA graphs on, concurrency 64, 64 distinct 768×768 images, 64 output tokens, greedy. Each arm was a fresh process start plus one warmup request, then two measured passes. Zero failed requests. The metadata proxy logged 129 rewrites; the raw proxy (`--no-rewrite`) logged 0.

| arm | pass | req/s | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| raw | cold | 5.46 | 349 | 7575 ms | 59.0 ms |
| raw | warm | 10.91 | 698 | 3573 ms | 31.0 ms |
| metadata-only | cold | 6.22 | 398 | 6530 ms | 50.1 ms |

Video throughput was rerun with `vllm bench serve` after the first 16-request burst proved to be one unschedulable wave (raw warm slower than raw cold, metadata cold dominated by a few multi-second prefills). This run is a different pod, same image and patch. Each arm is a fresh 1E+1PD process and a fresh EC cache. 64 distinct 2-second 320×240 clips at 8 fps, ShareGPT dataset, 64 output tokens, greedy, concurrency 8. One probe measured 248 prompt tokens, and 8192 / 248 caps concurrency at 8. Pass 1 is preceded by 8 warmups of the first clip so Triton JIT is outside the measurement. Pass 2 and pass 3 are repeats with no extra warmup. Zero failed requests. Mean TTFT stays next to the median, and P99 TTFT stays within about 1.5× the mean. The metadata proxy logged 201 rewrites; the raw proxy logged 0. On each paired pass, metadata-only is slightly ahead (about 1.07–1.11× output tok/s and 0.86–0.92× mean TTFT). Repeating a warm pass on the same arm moves output tok/s by 9–12%, which is the same size as that gap, so this table is not a video speedup claim.

| image | prompt tokens | answer text |

```bash
python3 -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/models/multimodal/processing \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py \
```

## Details

`Glm4vMultiModalDataParser.embedding_fields` marks the grid and video timestamps as placeholder metadata and the embeds as values, so `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` drops only the embeds on an EC consumer. Timestamps are computed with the existing GLM-5.3 frame sampler and stored on the processed video item, which is what the encoder publishes and what the prompt replacement reads. Image replacement was already grid-sized; it now works when the request carries only `image_grid_thw`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Use 64-bit row offsets in the Triton W4A16 GEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #63049. `triton_w4a16_gemm_kernel` indexes activations and outputs with int32 row offsets, which wrap once M × K or M × N passes 2^31 and fault on ROCm. Casting `pid_m` to int64 makes both products 64-bit. The weight, scale and zero-point offsets do not depend on M and stay int32.

## Test Plan

The new test runs the GEMM one block of rows past each bound, (K, N) = (256, 34816) for the output offsets and (17408, 256) for the activation offsets, and compares the last 64 rows with the float32 reference already in the file.

I also called `_triton_w4a16_gemm_impl` alone at a Qwen3.5 27B model's shapes, served `vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-AWQ` and `vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-GPTQ` at the default 262,144-token length on one MI300X, and timed the kernel before and after the change.

## Test Result

The new test passes, along with the rest of the file. Before the change the kernel faults at M = 62,000 with (K, N) = (5120, 34816) and at M = 124,000 with (17408, 5120). After it, both shapes run up to M = 262,144, and their last rows are as close to a float32 matmul as at small M. Both packages now serve at the default length, and their answers on 300 requests match those of runs at `--max-model-len 32768`, which did not reach the bound. Over three projection shapes, M from 1 to 32,768, with and without zero points, every timing is within 2.6% of the unchanged kernel, in both directions.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Leave GLM-4.7 array and object tool arguments unpinned
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The non-strict GLM-4.7 structural tag from #56403 pins array and object tool arguments to JSON. When GLM writes one of those values as text that is not valid JSON, the grammar forces tokens the model rates near zero, and the call can loop until `max_tokens`. This leaves array and object values as raw text, the way string values already are.

## Claims

- Only requests that get the non-strict GLM-4.7 tag change, and only in array and object arguments, plus type lists that contain them. These are `glm47` requests with tools (`tool_choice` auto, required or a named tool), and `ling3` requests with `required`, a named tool, or `--tool-strict-level function`. The value becomes text that ends at `</arg_value>`. Integer, number, boolean, null and enum values keep their JSON pins, and so do argument keys and the call envelope.
- A valid JSON value parses exactly as before. A value that is not JSON reaches the client as the raw string, through the parser's existing fallback (`coerce_to_schema_type`). On main the grammar rules such values out by forcing other tokens instead.
- Strict tools (`strict: true` or `--tool-strict-level parameter`) are unchanged. No other parser uses this tag.
- The change is in `_glm_4_7_value_format` only: 13 lines added and 10 removed, plus tests.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New tests | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -k container` | 2 failed, 6 passed | 8 passed |
| Registry tests | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py` | | 278 passed |
| GLM parser tests | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py` | | 42 passed |
| Structural-tag attach | `pytest tests/parser/test_abstract_parser.py` | | 10 passed |
| GLM-5.3 served by vLLM, 10 samples per arm (below) | | intended path 4/10; 6/10 corrupted; 3/10 hit the 120-token cap | intended path 10/10, all finished |

The two failing cases on main are the two texts the model really writes: a bare backslash (`D:\SVILUPPO\docs\PLAN.md`) and an over-escaped key quote (`[{"path\": ...`). Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` (xgrammar 0.2.8) with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. `ruff` 0.14.0 and the repo's `mypy` hook (1.20.2, Python 3.11) are clean.

<details>
<summary>GLM-5.3 A/B</summary>

The A/B runs on a GLM-5.3 deployment (vLLM 0.32.0, MTP with 3 speculative tokens). The prompt is a captured 5,400-token Cline request (Windows workspace, 26 tools, `tool_choice` auto), cut after the model's `</think>`. It is sent to `/v1/completions` with temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 and `max_tokens` 120, and the tag is passed in `structured_outputs.structural_tag`. The arms:

- No grammar.
- The tag main builds for the request.
- The tag this branch builds for the request. `ParserManager.get_parser("glm47", "glm45", enable_auto_tools=True)` and `adjust_request` on the branch give a tag equal to this arm's, field by field.

| Arm | Path written | Finished |
|---|---|---|
| No grammar | `D:\SVILUPPO\MantoRustPad\docs\TEAM\PROMPT_JUNIOR.md` 10/10 | 10/10 |
| main tag | correct 4/10 (written as escaped JSON); others `D:\b\bb0324-...\bb0324-...` repeating, `\test-chromium-mcp\test-chromium-mcp...`, `\bin\fake_shell_bin\...` | 7/10 |
| This PR's tag | `D:\SVILUPPO\MantoRustPad\docs\TEAM\PROMPT_JUNIOR.md` 10/10 | 10/10 |

The deployment's own tag-building code is main's. Not measured: a server running this branch end to end. The tag it builds is checked above, and the parser output for non-JSON values is covered by the existing fallback.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `_glm_4_7_value_format` returns `JSONSchemaFormat(json_schema={"type": t})` for every non-string type, arrays and objects included. Two things go wrong inside that element when the model's text is not JSON.

1. After a backslash inside a JSON string, the grammar admits only `" \ / b f n r t u`. GLM-5.3 writes Windows paths with single backslashes. On a captured request ending in `"path": "D:\`, the unconstrained next token is `SV` at p = 0.999998, and the grammar blocks all of the top 20 candidates. Sampling then picks a token the model rates below 1e-9 (`b`). The path fills with invented `\b...` and `\f...` names, and a 20-token cycle forms that top_p 0.95 cannot leave. With `max_tokens` unset, it runs to the context limit.
2. The JSON element has no excludes. When the model over-escapes a key's closing quote (`[{"newText\": ...`), the key string stays open, so `</arg_value>` and `</tool_call>` are read as string text and no stop token is allowed. In one captured turn the model wanted to stop (`<|observation|>` at p = 0.999993 unconstrained) and was forced on to 322 calls. If a later quote closes the key instead, the grammar allows only whitespace or `:`, and the output is whitespace until `max_tokens`.

We saw both in production with GLM-5.3 coding agents. In one afternoon we caught seven looping requests, and six of them were tool calls under this tag. Before #56403 these requests had no grammar. `--tool-strict-level auto` avoids the problem today by dropping the tag for non-strict auto requests, but that also drops the call-envelope constraint.

**Change.** A value keeps a JSON pin only when every type it allows is a scalar (`integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`). Anything else gets `AnyTextFormat(excludes=_GLM_4_7_VALUE_EXCLUDES)`, the format string values already use. That covers `array`, `object`, `string`, a missing type, and a type list that includes any of these. A type list with `string` was already free text in practice, because `OrFormat` with free text admits everything the JSON branch admits.

**Tradeoff.** In non-strict mode, array and object arguments lose their shape constraint. A model that writes malformed JSON there now gets it through as a string, which the client sees as an argument of the wrong type. Clients that need the shape enforced can mark the tool `strict: true`. This is the same contract string arguments have.

**Related.** #61205 (open) caps whitespace in these tags at 64 characters. That shortens the whitespace tail in case 2, but the grammar then forces `:` and the broken call continues. This PR removes the JSON element those runs happen in. The two PRs touch the same last line of `_glm_4_7_value_format`, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase. #62499 (open) changes when the tag applies alongside `response_format`, a different path. No open PR changes the GLM value formats.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the root-cause analysis, the fix, the tests and this description.

commits.pr_title: [CI][MoE] Start every MoE kernel test file from a clean GPU state
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix `:nvidia: (L4) MoE Kernels Shard 2/3` on main. It has failed on every run since [98366](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98366) (Oct 29, 15:44Z) and shows up as a failure on unrelated PRs (e.g. #64378):

```
FAILED kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py::test_modular_kernel_combinations_singlegpu  (x5)
torch.distributed.DistBackendError: NCCL error ... unhandled cuda error
ncclUnhandledCudaError: Call to CUDA function failed.
Last error: Failed to CUDA calloc async 608 bytes
```

**Root cause:** order dependence, exposed by a runtime-shard re-plan. No code change caused it.
- `tests/kernels/moe/conftest.py` turns off the per-test `cleanup_fixture` and cleans on entry only for files in `NEEDS_CLEAN_ENTRY` (or tests using `dist_init`). `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` is in neither, so it inherits whatever GPU memory earlier files left cached in the pytest process.
- The runtime-shard planner partitions files using timings from `ci.vllm.ai/api/timings/latest`. Between builds 98337 and 98366 the timing data refreshed. The test set was identical (11,004 tests), but the split changed from 2196/1653/7155 to 3941/1990/5073. That put `test_gpt_oss_triton_kernels.py` right before `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` in shard 2.
- The worker process the test spawns then cannot allocate even 608 bytes for NCCL setup on the 22 GiB L4.

No PR's CI could catch this, since the trigger was a timing-data refresh, not a diff.

**Fix:** keep the per-test speedup, but also clean once whenever pytest moves to a new file. That is about 40 cleanups per shard instead of about 1,450 per-test ones. No file then depends on what earlier files left behind, whatever order the planner chooses. The existing allowlist and `dist_init` behavior are unchanged.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this conftest or test.

## Test Plan

Not run locally (no GPU here). The L4 `MoE Kernels` shards on this PR will confirm. Note that the PR build may use a different shard plan, so the clearest confirmation is main going green after merge.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Fix Mamba region stride on block-outermost layouts
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix NIXL transfers of Mamba/SSM hybrid state on block-outermost KV cache layouts (`BLHNC`, `BLNHC`), and add a CPU test that pulls one request between two NIXL workers on real model KV layouts and checks every byte.

Related: vllm-project/vllm#63416 changes how NIXL pairs regions. This PR does not depend on it, and #63416 rebases onto it without conflicts.

## Claims

- **Fix.** With `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`, Qwen3-Next (GDN) and Nemotron-H (Mamba2) disaggregated P/D read the wrong Mamba state and wrote outside the request's blocks, with no error. They now transfer correctly. Layer-outermost layouts (the default) are unchanged. Hybrids whose attention is MLA, such as Kimi-Linear, were not affected (see Root cause).
- **Test.** The NIXL unit tests build KV cache configs and tensors by hand. The new test plans and allocates both sides with vLLM's own planner (`get_kv_cache_configs`) and allocator (`allocate_kv_cache`), from the per-layer KV specs of 12 models. D pulls one request from P through the real worker code; the recorded descriptors run as memory copies. Every page of every layer must land in D's block for the same layer and request position, and no other D byte may change.

## Validation

CPU only: `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`. No weights or model code: the KV specs are built in the test.

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k real_model
# 14 passed in ~10 s
```

| Case | KV plan in the test (groups → regions) | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B (same shape as GLM-4.5-Air, MiniMax-M2) | 4 full, 1 → 4 | auto (LBHNC) |
| gpt-oss-20b | SW + full, 2 → 2 shared | auto |
| Gemma 3 1B | 10 SW + 2 full, 6 → 2 shared | auto |
| MiMo-V2-Flash | 9 SW + 3 full, 4 → 3 shared | auto |
| DeepSeek-V3 (same as Kimi-K2) | 4 MLA, 1 → 4 | auto; BLNHC → BLNHC; BLNHC P → LBNHC D |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 | MLA + indexer cache, 1 → 8 | auto |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 6 GDN + 2 full, 4 → 2 shared | auto; BLHNC |
| NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 | 11 Mamba2 + 2 full, 7 → 2 shared | auto; BLHNC |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 6 KDA + 2 MLA, 4 → 2 shared | auto; BLNHC |

Fails before the fix: the new test with `main`'s `base_worker.py`:

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k "real_model and BLHNC"
FAILED ...[Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-BLHNC-BLHNC]
  AssertionError: ['model.layers.0.linear_attn[0].0', 'model.layers.4.linear_attn[0].0', ...]
FAILED ...[NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-BLHNC-BLHNC]
  AssertionError: ['model.layers.0.mixer[0].0', 'model.layers.11.mixer[0].0', ...]
2 failed
```

Every GDN/Mamba2 page arrives wrong. With the fix, all 14 cases pass.

The test also catches descriptor bugs it was not written for: dropping the conv-state offset from the peer's SSM descriptor (`_build_mamba_remote`) fails the three layer-outermost hybrid cases.

NIXL unit suites (`test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_push_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`), on `main` and on this branch:

| Tree | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` @ `4e0ad5720` | 646 | 4 |
| this branch | 660 | 4, the same ones |

- **The 4 failures on both:** `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma` needs a gated HF repo, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray, None]` needs Ray/GPU, and `test_register_packed_dsv4_mla_cache_as_single_region[v41-aliased-groups]` fails on `main` as well.
- **Transient failures:** the branch's first suite run also had 11 consecutive failures in `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, during a period of HF Hub rate limiting (see below). All 11 passed on rerun, and a full run of that file passed (271 tests).

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

Note on flakiness: the new test builds two `create_vllm_config` configs per case, as other NIXL unit tests do. When the HF Hub rate-limits the `facebook/opt-125m` file listing (HTTP 429), any of these tests fails in setup. That was the only failure cause seen in about 600 local runs of the new test.

## Details

**Root cause.** Under the hybrid KV cache manager, cache groups share KV cache tensors. With a block-outermost layout, block *b* of every tensor sits side by side in one row, so a layer's view advances by the row: 4,718,592 B for Qwen3-Next's two tensors in the test, not by one 2,359,296 B page. `register_kv_caches` registered Mamba regions with `block_stride = physical_page_size` and took the view's stride only for CSA-linear. So every Mamba descriptor past block 0 pointed into the other tensor's pages. Attention regions on the same rows already used the view stride.

Only some hybrids hit it. A shared region keeps the stride of the first layer registered into it (layer-name order), and a later layer replaces it only if it is MLA. Mamba sub-region descriptors use the region's stride:
- In Qwen3-Next and Nemotron-H a Mamba layer comes first, and their full-attention layers never replace its page stride.
- In Kimi-Linear the MLA layer replaces it with the row stride, so its KDA descriptors were right by accident; the Kimi-Linear BLNHC case passes with or without the fix.

The fix takes the view's stride for Mamba views on block-outermost layouts too. Elsewhere the page stride stays. A view indexed by kernel block (several per logical block) has a stride of a fraction of the page, and taking the view's stride there breaks the existing hetero-block-size tests.

Flow (pull, the failing case):
1. Startup, P and D: `register_kv_caches` registers each region as `(base, len, stride, count)`; Mamba regions get stride = one page.
2. Handshake: D builds descriptors for P's Mamba sub-regions (conv q/k/v parts, SSM state) from P's metadata, and its own from its local regions.
3. Read: a descriptor id for block *b* resolves to `base + b × stride`. With stride = page instead of row, block *b*'s address lands in another tensor's page of a lower block, on both sides.

**The test.**
- Models are those tested end to end for vllm-project/vllm#63416. MiniMax-M1 is left out; vLLM removed it in 0.23.0.
- Specs mirror what each model's layers return. Nine were dumped from a meta-device model build on CPU. DeepSeek-V3.2 (sparse MLA + indexer) and Kimi-Linear (MLA + KDA) cannot be built on CPU, so their specs come from their configs and vLLM's state-shape helpers.
- Each case uses the first layers of its model, enough for its group and region pattern (2 regions for the hybrids). The largest case allocates about 120 MB per side.
- Hybrid block sizes are the ones vLLM aligns to on CPU (1152, 1408). For Kimi-Linear it is 1920, the first 64-token multiple whose MLA page holds the KDA state.

**Not covered.**
- Push, TP mismatch, PP stages, and P and D with different settings. With the same model and settings the region pairing is the identity; those cases stay with the hand-built tests.
- GPU, and an end-to-end P/D run with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` on a hybrid model.

**Mocks.** `tests/AGENTS.md` asks for real objects. The workers are patched the same way as the existing `_make_mla_hybrid_worker` helper in this file:
- the platform reports a CUDA device, so the GPU registration path runs on a CPU host;
- attention backends and kernel block-size selection are faked, since no model layers are built;
- TP rank and size are fixed at 0 and 1;
- NIXL itself is the file's `_RecordingNixl`.

Planner, allocator, layout resolution, registration, handshake and descriptor code are all real.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#62453 fixes Mamba page padding on the CPU host-buffer path, and vllm-project/vllm#64140 fixes packed Mamba addressing in the KV offloading worker. Neither touches NIXL's Mamba region stride.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Parser] Parse closed GLM-4.7 tool arguments once while streaming
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A GLM tool call that repeats closed argument pairs makes `Glm47MoeParser` re-parse every pair on each streaming conversion, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call until the event loop saturates and liveness fails. This parses each closed pair once. Follow-up to #61253, which covers a single long open value.

## Claims

- Streaming a call with N closed pairs matches the argument regex N times in total. On main every conversion matches all closed pairs again: 1,345,003 matches for N = 401 in the new test.
- Streamed deltas and non-streaming results are unchanged.
- No new config, flag or API. Scope is the `glm47` tool parser; `Ling3Parser` gets the `>` gate only (see Details).

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `24e80c2614` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py::TestStreamedToolArguments::test_closed_pairs_are_parsed_once` | `AssertionError: assert 1345003 == 401` | passed |
| GLM parser tests | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py` | 22 passed, 1 failed (the new test) | 23 passed |
| Parser suite | `pytest tests/parser --ignore=tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py --ignore=tests/parser/test_harmony.py` | 6660 passed, 3 failed | 6661 passed, 2 failed |
| Looping stream replay (below) | GLM-5.3 tokenizer, 200 tok/s, liveness 30 s / 5 s / 3 | liveness kill at 275 s | no kill in 1200 s, loop 0-7% busy at 240K tokens |

Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The 2 parser-suite failures left are in `tests/parser/mistral/test_reasoning.py` and fail the same on main: the image ships mistral-common 1.11.6 and main needs 1.13.0 (#64169). The two ignored files fail collection in that image for the same reason and for a harmony download. `ruff` 0.14.0 and the repo's `mypy` hook (1.20.2, Python 3.11) are clean on both files.

Also checked on `glm47_moe.py`:
- The resumed parse equals a fresh parse on 541,418 random argument texts grown piece by piece (3 seeds), with tag fragments, repeated keys, and a second call reusing the cache.
- Streamed output with the real GLM-5.3 tokenizer through `ParserManager.get_parser("glm47", "glm45")`: 11 streams (edits, long writes, open values, typed and array arguments, repeated keys, two calls, plain content) at chunk sizes 1, 3, 4, 7 and 64, plus non-streaming. Content, reasoning, names, arguments and argument-delta counts are identical to the unpatched parser (vLLM `d6394cf758`, same `glm47_moe.py` and argument path as main) in 66 of 66 cases.

Not measured: an end-to-end server run with a GLM checkpoint.

<details>
<summary>Looping stream replay</summary>

The replay feeds one GLM-5.3 output through the streaming parser on a virtual clock. The engine emits 200 tokens/s in 4-token steps (MTP at full acceptance). Each event-loop pass hands every token emitted since the previous pass to one `parse_delta` call. Measured parser time is doubled for a slower server CPU, and kubelet liveness (30 s period, 5 s timeout, 3 failures) is replayed on those passes. The output is `</think><tool_call>Edit`, a `file_path` pair, then `old_string` / `new_string` pairs repeated.

| Stream time | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 27 s, 5.4K tokens | loop 24% busy | 0% |
| 114 s, 22.8K tokens | 99% | 1% |
| 210-270 s | liveness fails 3 of 3 (25-58 s waits), kill at 275 s | 1% |
| 1200 s, 240K tokens, 1.46M chars | | 7% |

Once the loop saturates, each pass merges more tokens and each merged event converts again, so passes keep getting longer. The last pass on main merged 6,608 tokens, ran 7,267 conversions and took 62.9 s.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` converts the whole raw argument text whenever the open-value extender from #61253 is inactive: between arguments, and while the open key repeats an earlier key (the extender needs the open value to be the last JSON value). GLM set no `arg_structural_chars`, so every argument chunk event converted, and `_glm47_parse_args` re-ran `_ARG_RE.finditer` over every closed pair plus `_ARG_RE.sub` over the whole text. Merging deltas under load does not bound this, because conversions scale with the events in the merged text.

We hit this serving GLM-5.3 on vLLM 0.32.0, which includes #61253. Decode API servers climbed from 0.3 to 1 core in 3-4 minutes and failed liveness, five times in 24 hours. In three of them the logs show a single request left on the pod, generating at 99-100% MTP draft acceptance (the model repeating itself) while the stats line slipped from 10 s to 15-40 s apart. Stream content was not captured in production; the replay reproduces the same failure through the parser.

**Change.**
- `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, as DeepSeek V3.2 and V4 use. A delta without `>` cannot close a key or value, so it cannot produce a streamable change: an open last value goes through the extender, and an open repeated key sits mid-JSON where the prefix check withholds it. The next conversion or the final flush converts the full text. The gate alone only delays the kill in the replay (305 s against 215 s, measured on `d6394cf758`), because each conversion still re-scans.
- `_glm47_parse_args` takes an optional `_ClosedArgs` cache, and `Glm47MoeParser` binds one per instance into its converter and extender, the same way DeepSeek V4 and MiniMax M3 replace `_arg_converter` after `super().__init__`. A text that extends the cached text resumes after its last closed pair. Any other text parses from the start, and the cache moves forward whenever a scan closes a new pair. Appending text cannot change a pair that already closed, since each match ends at the first `</arg_value>` after its key, so resuming is exact.

**Cost.** What stays linear in the text per conversion is C-level work: `startswith` against the cached text, the slice when a pair closes, and the join of text outside the pairs for the open-key search. That is the 7% at 1.46M chars above.

**Compatibility and limits.**
- A parser built with a custom `arg_converter` keeps the uncached path (identity check in `__init__`), so tests that wrap the converter still see every call.
- `Ling3Parser` calls `ParserEngine.__init__` directly, so it gets the gate from the shared config and no cache.
- A looping call still generates until `max_tokens`; this keeps the server responsive while it does.
- Unchanged here and the same on main: when a repeated key closes with a different value than before, the final JSON no longer extends what was streamed and the flush withholds it, so the client gets truncated arguments. I can file that separately.

**Not a duplicate.** #61253 (merged) covers one long open value. #58418 (open) edits `_glm47_parse_args` for an unclosed final value; the overlap is textual only. #51141 and #64196 address Inkling and DeepSeek DSML. No open PR covers re-parsing closed GLM pairs.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the root-cause analysis, the fix, the tests and this description.

## Overview

`TestIdleWhileServingPeers` (both tests) fails on main:

```
FAILED v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestIdleWhileServingPeers::test_pinned_peer_hit_does_not_block_idleness - assert <LookupResult.MISS: 1> is <LookupResult.RETRY: 4>

```

It is a merge race between two PRs that each passed CI on their own:

- #64501 made a probe `lookup()` return `MISS` until the peer acks the handshake (`p2p/manager.py:440`), so the request prefills locally instead of waiting.
- #63618 added these tests on a base without #64501. Its `_peer_hit` helper probes right after `on_new_request` and asserts `RETRY`.

## Fix

Test-only. `_peer_hit` probes only once the consumer session to the peer exists and is ready, and keeps driving both managers until then. Other probe tests drain a fixed number of times before probing; polling until the deadline also covers the poll-thread case, where the producer answers asynchronously. The #64501 behavior is intended and unchanged.

## Validation

No local GPU/runtime environment, so validation is through CI:

- Before (main): the `v1-kv-offload` step fails with the two errors above, e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98388#01a188c1-0e2b-46c5-91f3-0e4141da6244 (`55b677b2d1`).
- After (this PR, `da37fb81cf`): the same step (`pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload`, `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`) passes: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98413#01a18905-afb0-4c8c-aae2-d582a5f0be49

No model evals: test-only change.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `TestIdleWhileServingPeers`, `_peer_hit`, `test_pinned_peer_hit`, and PRs referencing #63618 / #64501: none.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode at TP8 on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Mono decode (`--monokernel`) for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs only at TP2 and TP4. `MonoDecodeLayer._create` refuses any other tensor-parallel size. At conc 1 a TP8 server can still use mono decode: each rank streams half the weights, while the persistent K1/K2 chain stays the same length. This PR makes the existing FlyDSL kernels correct at TP8 on gfx950. That means 8 attention heads per rank, and a 288-wide routed/shared expert intermediate (routed is padded to 384 by the loader).

At TP8 the only kernel changes are the head-tile rounding and one GEMV tail. The cross-rank reduction, MoE, router, K1 front, combine and draft runner already loop over `tp` and need no changes.

## Changes

- `mono/attention/plan.py`, `Dims`: `head_tiles` now rounds up (`cdiv(heads, 16)`), and a new `heads_pad` gives whole tiles. Before this, `head_tiles` was `8 // 16 = 0` at TP8, so the split-attention loops (`back.py`) emitted no MFMAs and would silently produce wrong output once the gate opens.
  - At M=7, ratio 2, the CPU compile for gfx950 shows 0 bf16 MFMAs before the fix and 32 after, the same count as TP4.
  - A rank must have at least one tile; this is asserted.
- `mono/attention/back.py`: the split stage's q/p/st LDS and the stat offset are sized by `heads_pad`. The padded head columns are computed but never stored. That is correct by column independence:
  - each head has its own score max and its own PV column;
  - the stat stores and the combine read only `h < heads`.
- `mono/stages/gemv.py`: the row-major FP8 step load accepts `K % 64 == 32`, which is the shared expert's down projection at K = 288. The last step's upper lanes are clamped into the row, and `_fp8_step_mfma` already zeroes them on both sides.
- `mono_decode.py`: the gate admits TP8. gfx942 stays TP4 only (`:410`).
- Tests: TP8 cases are added to `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` (`tp in [2, 4, 8]`) and `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (`(8, 8)` and `(8, 28)` on cdna4).

## Test Plan

1. CPU-only FlyDSL compile for gfx950 (AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0), on this branch and on unmodified main:
   - TP8 builds: K1, K2 and FFN at M = 7 and 28; ratios 0, 1 and 2; the index-source and fold variants; and the DSpark draft K1/K2.
   - TP2 and TP4 builds: compared byte for byte against main.
2. GPU, 8x MI355X: a TP8 server with `--monokernel` running the MLPerf conc-1 recipe:
   - DSpark k=6;
   - adaptive verification off;
   - decoder SWA bounded replay;
   - MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer.

   Measurements:
   - `vllm bench serve`, random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic acceptance length 3.87, so the step time is isolated from acceptance;
   - GSM8K-1319, 8-shot greedy, block rejection with real acceptance, on the same server.
3. To run on this branch with 8 GPUs:
   ```
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py -k "8"
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -k "8-8 or 8-28"
   ```

## Test Result

**CPU compile:** every TP8 build compiles with 0 VGPR spills, scratch 0, and LDS ≤ 137,248 B. TP2 and TP4 kernel binaries are byte-identical to main.

| Build | VGPR | LDS (B) |
|---|---|---|
| TP8 K1, M=7 | 142 | 38,944 |
| TP8 K2, M=7 (ratio 1/2, index) | 250 | 96,640 |
| TP8 K2, M=28 | 232 | 137,248 |
| TP8 FFN, M=7 | 243 | 79,408 |
| TP8 draft K2, M=6 | 199 | 96,640 |

**GPU, this PR alone:**
- Image: nightly `5d35ce3934` + this PR, with none of the other open DSv4.1 PRs. `mono/` and `mono_decode.py` are identical to this PR's base.
- Setup: one TP8 server with the MLPerf conc-1 recipe, `--monokernel` on or off and nothing else changed.

Decode step: random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic AL 3.87; ITL p50 is one DSpark step.

| TP8 | c1 step | c1 tok/s | c4 step | c4 TPOT | c4 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--monokernel` (this PR) | **5.36 ms** | 580 | **8.10 ms** | 2.57 ms | 1163 |
| without | 8.59 ms | 392 | 10.10 ms | 3.38 ms | 1014 |
| change | **-37.5%** | +48% | **-19.8%** | -24% | +15% |

Quality, same servers, real (block) acceptance:

| TP8 | GSM8K-1319 (2 runs) | AL | RULER NIAH 32k (8 tasks x 50) | RULER NIAH 128k (8 tasks x 25) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--monokernel` | 0.910 / 0.910 | 3.562 / 3.587 | 0.997 | 0.993 |
| without | 0.923 / 0.923 | 3.563 / 3.593 | 0.998 | 0.990 |

- GSM8K: mono on vs off is a paired McNemar of 26/44 flips (p 0.041) and 28/45 (p 0.060). The same arm run twice gives 35/35 and 33/32.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Quantization] NVFP4 MoE re-quantization and fused shared experts through online quantization
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Second PR of the split of #63232, stacked on #64111. Its base is `minimax-m31-flash-model`, so only this PR's commit shows up; it will be retargeted to `main` after #64111 merges. The change lets ROCm serve NVFP4-expert checkpoints such as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: the routed experts are re-quantized to MXFP4/MXFP8 at load. It also makes fused shared experts (FSE) work with online quantization.

## Claims

- **NVFP4 MoE re-quantization without an NVFP4 backend:** main can already re-quantize serialized NVFP4 MoE (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark) to an online MoE method. This PR makes that work where no NVFP4 MoE backend exists (ROCm):
  - The NVFP4 oracle skips backend selection for layers whose checkpoint method only serves as the dequantization source (`requantization_source_scope`).
  - `dequantize_weight` for MoE now yields `(experts, w13, w2)` per group of experts, which bounds the staging memory.
- **FSE with online quantization:** `OnlineSharedExpertLoader` stages the shared expert at load and quantizes it into its routed slot after loading. It replaces `RoutedExperts._fused_shared_expert_quantizer`, which only handled full-precision shared experts. Supported combinations:
  - NVFP4 routed experts re-quantized to MXFP4, with the shared expert re-quantized to the same scheme;
  - Quark MXFP4 routed experts (kept as stored) with an MXFP8 shared expert quantized to MXFP4 online.

  FSE is refused with a warning when the shared and routed experts would not run with the same `(weight, activation)` keys. Two cases raise `NotImplementedError`: BF16 routed experts quantized online combined with a quantized shared expert, and reloading weights with FSE.
- **MiniMax-M3 on ROCm:** a clear error for the NVFP4-expert checkpoint unless the routed experts are re-quantized (`--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` or `mxfp8`).
- **Two small ROCm fixes from the same branch:**
  - gfx942: the online FP8 PTPC MoE quantizes W13 in torch, because `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` can crash there during load.
  - The MXFP8 Triton activation quant uses a tuned block size for M == 1.

## Validation

Pre-commit passes, including mypy (Python 3.11) on all changed files.

Unit tests were run on GB300 (CUDA) for this branch and for #64111 (its base) in the same environment. The changed and new tests pass; the failures were identical on both branches (table below).

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py tests/quantization/test_fp8_per_channel.py \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_emulation.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py
```

| | this PR | #64111 |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 656 | 646 |
| skipped | 86 | 54 |
| failed | 27 | 27 (the same tests) |

- The 10 extra passes are this PR's new tests.
- The 32 extra skips are the ROCm-only tests in `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py`.
- The 27 shared failures are environmental: engine start-up on GPUs shared with other jobs (about 10 GB free), a Triton "PTX compiled with an unsupported toolchain" error in this environment, and one out-of-memory error. Three `test_modelopt` failures also fail on `main` here.

Not covered:
- `tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` holds most of the coverage of this PR (NVFP4 routed × online targets × FSE for compressed-tensors and Quark, Quark MXFP4 routed + MXFP8 shared, NVFP4 oracle skip). It is ROCm-only, and its CI jobs are disabled (`tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`: pending locked torchao dependencies). I did not run it: there is no AMD hardware here.
- No ROCm end-to-end run on this branch. The code comes from the AMD contributors' branch (#63232).

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** #63547 (draft) also serves the NVFP4 M3.1 checkpoint on AMD, but converts NVFP4 → MXFP4 inside the model (`minimax_m3/common/nvfp4_mxfp4.py`). This PR goes through the generic online quantization API instead, so it applies to any ModelOpt, compressed-tensors or Quark NVFP4 MoE and supports FSE.
- **Shared code touched (all at load time, no forward-path change):**
  - `resolve_quant_method` builds the checkpoint method of re-quantized experts under `requantization_source_scope`.
  - `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` returns the emulation backend inside that scope.
  - `QuantizeMethodBase.dequantize_weight` returns an iterator for MoE. All three MoE implementations (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark NVFP4) and the one caller are migrated.
  - `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` and `load_weights` route shared-expert slots through the loader.
  - `process_weights_after_loading` finalizes the staged shared experts. It is a no-op unless FSE and online quantization are both used.
  - `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` now compares the effective `(weight, activation)` keys of the routed and shared experts.
  - `QuarkLinearMethod.dequantize_weight` supports MXFP8.
- **Conflicts with main:** main's #61457 (per-layer FSE selection) landed after the source branch. I kept main's `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert`. The source branch's extra warning, for `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` set without AITER MoE, was dropped: it also fires on CUDA, where AITER is unavailable.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/quantization/online.md` already documents NVFP4 MoE re-quantization; FSE with online quantization is not documented yet.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to port these changes from #63232 and resolve the conflicts with main. The original code is by fxmarty-amd (re-quantization + FSE), andyluo7 (gfx942 FP8) and hongxiayang (MXFP8 M=1), credited in the commit. The submitter reviewed the port and ran the tests above.
