commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Renew prefill KV leases from the decoder
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Today the Mooncake prefiller holds a finished request's KV until the decoder pulls it, or until `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (480 s) runs out. This PR adds an opt-in `kv_lease_duration` that replaces that fixed timeout with a lease the decoder renews, following NixlConnector's lease (#41383, [design](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md)). It addresses the "480s expire fallback" in item 6 of RFC #60523. ## Claims - **D crash:** P frees the dead decoder's KV within one lease of D's last renewal, instead of after 480 s. - **D overload:** requests queued on a busy decoder keep their KV for as long as they wait. A short fixed timeout fails them. - **Late pulls:** a pull for KV that P has already freed fails at once, instead of waiting out the timeout. This also applies when the lease is off. - Without `kv_lease_duration`, behavior is unchanged. ## Validation **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py` → 144 passed (A800, `huggingface_hub==1.31.0` as in CI). The new tests use the real scheduler, real ZMQ sockets and a stubbed bootstrap service. They cover: - renewal is off without the option, and throttled to every `lease / 6` with it; - D renews until the pull settles or the request aborts; - renewals reach every paired P worker, querying the bootstrap first if needed; - on P, renewals extend only known transfers and never shorten a deadline, and a P without the lease rejects them; - pulls on the same channel still work; - a pull for freed KV gets an immediate error. `pre-commit` passes. **End to end:** 2× A800 with 200G HDR IB, Mooncake TE 0.3.13.post1, DeepSeek-MoE-16B, TP=1 per side. Both sides run main `10e8e921b`, with only `mooncake_connector.py` swapped (baseline vs this PR). - Load: 128 requests, 3,000-token prompts, 1,000 output tokens. That is 2.4× D's KV capacity, so D always has a queue. - Probe: a 512-token request sent straight to P every 10 s. | Case | Unmodified main | This PR | |---|---|---| | **A.** D killed at t≈23 s; 480 s timeout vs 30 s lease | P's KV stays at 99% until t≈484 s; the probe sent at t≈10 s takes 475.5 s | P's KV is below 5% at t≈103 s; that probe takes 61.3 s, later probes 36–46 ms | | **B.** No crash, requests wait on D up to ~80 s; 20 s timeout vs 20 s lease | 79 / 128 requests fail | 128 / 128 succeed, no lease expires | In case A, requests still queued on P when D died are prefilled afterwards. The baseline holds them for another 480 s, and P is still at 37% KV when the run ends at t=660 s. The lease holds each for one 30 s lease.
Reproduction ```bash # Same on D with "kv_role":"kv_consumer" and --port 8020. Drop kv_lease_duration for the baseline; # case B's baseline sets VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=20 on both sides. vllm serve deepseek-ai/deepseek-moe-16b-chat --port 8010 --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code \ --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"device_name":"mlx5_102","kv_lease_duration":30}}' python examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \ --port 8000 --prefill http://

:8010 8998 --decode http://:8020 ``` - Load: 128 streaming completions sent at once through the proxy, each with random prompt token ids, `max_tokens=1000` and `ignore_eos`. - Probe: a plain completion with `max_tokens=1`, sent to P without `kv_transfer_params`. - Case A sends `SIGKILL` to D's process group 20 s after the load starts.

**Overhead:** - P checks each side-channel message for a renewal: 0.7 µs for a steady pull, 1.3 µs for a pull carrying the layout, 21 µs for an 18 KB pull of 32 requests. - D sends one message of about 1 KB per 128 transfer ids, to each paired P worker every `lease / 6`. ## Details **Flow** 1. D starts tracking a request in `on_new_request`, while it may still be queued. 2. Every `lease / 6`, `build_connector_meta` groups the tracked transfer ids by P engine. 3. `start_load_kv` sends them to each P worker that D would pull from. 4. P sets `expire_time = now + lease` when prefill ends. On each renewal it sets `expire_time = max(expire_time, now + 2/3 · lease)`. 5. D stops renewing on `finished_recving` or `request_finished`. 6. When renewals stop, P frees the blocks on its next scan and remembers the transfer id, so a later pull fails at once. **Design notes** - **Opt-in, unlike NIXL.** Mooncake has no handshake compatibility check, so an old decoder paired with a lease-enabled prefiller would silently lose the KV of requests queued longer than the lease. The docs say to set the same value on both sides and to upgrade prefillers first. An old prefiller rejects renewals, and D warns once. - **Transport.** Renewals use P's existing ZMQ ROUTER, so there is no new port and the pull format is unchanged. - A pull decodes as an empty renewal, because msgspec skips unknown fields. - P's listener answers renewals itself, since all sender workers may be blocked waiting for prefills. - D waits for the reply, because a `linger=0` socket drops unsent messages. - Renewals go to the same P workers as the pull, using the address selection now shared with `receive_kv`. A P engine that D has not contacted yet gets a bootstrap query first. - **Expiry scan.** P keeps scanning every entry, because renewals reorder deadlines; NIXL's ordered reaper hit this in #58222. Deadlines never cross processes, so there is no clock skew (cf. #50326). - **Limitation.** Backpressure is unchanged: P holds KV for as long as a slow decoder needs it. In case B with the lease, P sits at 99% for about 40 s and a probe waits 35 s. The 20 s timeout frees KV sooner (probe 17 s) only by failing requests. Fixing that needs D-side staging (rd2h / host receive). - **#57530 failure spine.** With the lease on, P's deadline is the lease. `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` still bounds the wait for an unfinished prefill and how long freed transfer ids are remembered. **Not a duplicate.** I searched for Mooncake lease, heartbeat, `ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` and `expire_time`. #63420 and #59522 are leases in the Mooncake Store connector. #63804 is an external connector, and #57529 is a standalone failure ledger. Open PRs on this file (#62657, #62658, #62255, #61974) do not change P's expiry. **AI assistance:** written with Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line, ran all tests and experiments above, and can answer for the design. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Guard NaN scores in gfx942 mono routing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On gfx942, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--monokernel` and adaptive DSpark verification dies with `Memory access fault` during CUDA graph capture. The profile replays a context over KV blocks no request has written. The draft FFN then sees NaN router scores. `stage_route` ranks with `fx.max`, which keeps the NaN, so the same expert is picked twice and a later gather indexes off the slot table.

A NaN score now ranks last, and the winner ballot ignores lanes past the expert count. Both edits are in this patch. The KV fill is gone.

## Claims

- Without this patch, the serve command faults during the real capture and the server does not start.
- With both router edits and no KV zero, the real capture finishes and the server starts.
- Finite scores pick the same experts. TPOT on the shapes below stays with stock.
- No config or API change.

## Validation

MI325X, 4 GPUs, gfx942. The fault is on current main. The runs below are nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56` with main's Python over it, including this `stage_route`. The binaries were not rebuilt from this tree.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --monokernel --max-model-len 266240 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.9,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5],"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

| | without this patch | with this patch |
|---|---|---|
| real capture | `Memory access fault` on all four ranks after the DSpark graphs | finished in 60 s, 14.30 GiB |
| startup | engine core failed | `Application startup complete` |
| one completion | n/a | `Paris. The final answer is 123` |

Accuracy is a separate serve: monokernel, no speculative decoding. lm-eval `niah_single_1` at 4096, the first 8 of the 500 repeat-haystack samples. Stock and this patch both scored 1.0, and the 8 completions were identical.

Perf is that same serve, temperature 0, seed 0, 4 warmups. Mean / median TPOT:

| ISL / OSL / concurrency | prompts | stock | this patch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 / 128 / 4 | 64 | 5.43 / 5.23 ms | 5.42 / 5.23 ms |
| 1024 / 256 / 8 | 48 | 6.95 / 6.91 ms | 6.92 / 6.87 ms |
| 512 / 512 / 16 | 32 | 9.26 / 9.32 ms | 9.20 / 9.26 ms |

`stage_route` runs once per decode token. A longer prompt adds attention on every step, so these short prompts are where that cost can show up in TPOT. The output lengths are how many decode steps were averaged.

## Details

`batches_to_profile` is the only caller that passes a nonzero `context_len` into `_dummy_run`. `set_dummy_context` fills block tables with ids nobody has written, and the draft reads them. Two requests replay 10 tokens, the gfx942 monokernel's multi-tile draft FFN, and that launch faults.

`fx.max` keeps a NaN, and the NaN then compares equal to itself, so the draft shape emits the same expert id twice. The route counts winners with a bitmap, the count comes up short, and the gather reads off the slot table. Ranking the NaN as `-inf` after the max, and masking the ballot with `cursor < ept`, removes the duplicate. Kimi-K3 and MiniMax-M3 already drop NaN scores before ranking. The ballot mask is particular to this router, which holds 2 experts per lane and picks 3.

A local ranking check matches that. Unguarded draft NaN rows pick `[[0, 64, 0], [0, 64, 0]]`, bitmap 28 against 30 slots. With both edits the bitmap is 30 and there are no duplicates. Finite draft scores, and the target 384/6 shape, match with and without the guard. That check is the ranking logic, not the GPU kernel.

`stage_route` runs on every monokernel FFN launch, including target-only decode with adaptive verification off. The TPOT rows are that path.

Warmup and `profile_run` leave `context_len` at 0. `set_dcp_capture_context` is the other fabrication, only when `cp_size > 1`, and this PR does not change it.

`test_nan_draft_route_stays_in_range` launches that draft shape with NaN logits. With this patch it finishes, and each token's ids are unique:

```text

1 passed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings in 7.91s
```

Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: 0x44a297b0) on address 0x7ece472b5000. Reason: Unknown.
Fatal Python error: Aborted
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/accelerator/__init__.py", line 270 in synchronize
  File "/root/vllm/tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_mono_gfx942.py", line 732 in test_nan_draft_route_stays_in_range
EXIT:134

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share Engram host tables as host-NUMA cuMem across DP ranks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `dp_shared_memory`, node-local DP ranks share one registered `/dev/shm` mapping for the Engram host tables (2 layers x 94.4 GiB on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Lookups are random row reads and on GB200 they are bound by GPU TLB misses: the registered mapping uses 64K pages.

This PR allocates the shared table as host-NUMA cuMem instead, which the GPU maps with 2M pages. Rank 0 creates it on its GPU's NUMA node and broadcasts FABRIC handles; the other node-local DP ranks import and map them. Where FABRIC handles are unavailable (probed once: create + export), the existing `/dev/shm` path is used and logged.

Allocation never OOMs; it falls back instead:

- Rank 0 allocates in 2 GiB chunks and stops once its NUMA node would drop below a 5% reserve. Freed cuMem pages stay in the driver's page pool (`NVreg_EnableSystemMemoryPools`), which this estimate does not count, so reusing them after a restart is not penalized.
- The driver allocates with `__GFP_RETRY_MAYFAIL | __GFP_THISNODE`: the kernel compacts for 2M pages and fails the allocation rather than invoking the OOM killer. It never falls back to small pages.
- Any create, export, import or map failure on any rank releases everything on every rank, logs a warning, and falls back to `/dev/shm`.

Two `/dev/shm` fixes, since that path is now the fallback:

- **Orphaned tables:** rank 0 used to unlink the backing file only after every peer had registered it, and registration faults in the whole table. A rank killed in that window left a fully populated 94 GiB file in `/dev/shm` that nothing owned. Every rank now opens the file first, rank 0 unlinks it while it is still sparse, and only then do ranks mmap and register.
- **OOM kills:** `check_shm_free_space` only checks tmpfs capacity. A table larger than available host memory was faulted in anyway and the OOM killer made room. `/dev/shm` sharing now also requires the tables to fit in available host memory (cgroup-aware; `get_available_memory`, moved from `weight_utils` to `cpu_resource_utils`), both when sharing is decided and before allocating. The pre-check requires this even where cuMem will be used, so a per-layer fallback always has room.
- **NUMA binding:** under `--numa-bind` (`numactl --membind`), the fallback is most likely exactly when the GPU's node is full, and the membind confined the `/dev/shm` pages to that node, so the OOM killer fired despite free memory on the other node. The mapping now gets `mbind(MPOL_LOCAL)`: local node first, then any node.

Lookups only sort rows when the table has small (64K) pages. Sorting was keyed on "no THP", so cuMem tables were sorted too, which only adds the sort.

Files:

- New NVIDIA-only `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/engram_host_table.py` holds all cuMem code, including the create/broadcast/import protocol (`share_host_table`).
- `common/engram.py` (shared with ROCm): `DPSharedEngramStorage` keeps its interface. On CUDA it tries `share_host_table` first, behind an `is_cuda()` check and a lazy import; ROCm goes straight to `/dev/shm` as before. The `/dev/shm` fixes are platform-neutral and apply to ROCm too. The startup log says `via cuMem` or `via /dev/shm`.
- No new config option.

Not a duplicate: open Engram PRs cover pinned sizing (#59849), SP/PCP sharing (#57195, #61553), Mooncake and disk offload (#57023, #62238); none changes the shared host table backing.

## Performance

### Forward (GB200)

GB200, DEP4, `--numa-bind`-equivalent binding (`numactl` per rank), dummy weights, uniformly random tokens. Same node, back-to-back A/B. Measured before the sort change, i.e. with cuMem lookups still sorted from 1536 tokens.

Engram lookup, one layer, fresh ids every iteration:

| tokens | /dev/shm | cuMem |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 69 us | 49 us |
| 128 | 184 us | 90 us |
| 1024 | 1.21 ms | 0.47 ms |
| 4096 | 3.78 ms | 1.21 ms |
| 32768 | 9.92 ms | 4.36 ms |

`vllm bench forward` (median per-rank forward):

| case | /dev/shm | cuMem | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prefill 32768 | 346.76 ms | 333.93 ms | -3.7% |
| prefill 4 x 8192 | 347.18 ms | 333.65 ms | -3.9% |
| prefill 4 x 8192 @ 16384 ctx | 353.86 ms | 338.71 ms | -4.3% |
| prefill 16384 | 181.99 ms | 170.87 ms | -6.1% |
| prefill 4096 | 56.72 ms | 50.87 ms | -10.3% |
| decode 64 @ 16384 | 16.61 ms | 16.61 ms | 0% |
| decode 128 @ 16384 | 17.10 ms | 17.10 ms | 0% |

Decode lookups already overlap on the side stream. Real text repeats 15-22% of rows, so real prefill gains should be somewhat smaller than the random-token numbers.

```bash

commits.pr_title: [Perf][EPLB][DSv4] Add a symm_mem weight-migration backend and fuse MegaMoE replica mapping
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things:

- adds an opt-in `symm_mem` weight-migration backend;
- fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the DeepGEMM MegaMoE staging kernels;
- takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path.

Not a duplicate. No open or merged PR adds a symmetric-memory EPLB backend or fuses the MegaMoE mapping. #61176 and #61839 enable EPLB for the ROCm AITER MegaMoE backend. Related: #61767 (`cpu_all_reduce_`, reused here), #57549, #56716, #61643. #61395 (EPLB for the V4.1 DSpark draft) runs together with this PR in the GB300 validation.

## Claims

- With this PR and #61395, EPLB raises DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode throughput on GB300 NVL72 by +12.0% at DEP16 and +25.0% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank, and by +26.2% at DEP32 with 128 req/rank. At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, main-model MegaMoE drops from 14.7 to 7.6 ms per step. Earlier GB200 runs on an older build showed smaller gains; see Validation.
- `symm_mem`: senders push expert rows into the receiver's `expert_buffer`, which is allocated in CUDA symmetric memory. There is no staging buffer, and it needs no memory beyond `expert_buffer`. Cross-node peer copies run at about 800 GB/s, against about 88 GB/s for NIXL, and a 40-layer rearrangement transfers in 0.3–0.6 s at DEP32.
- MegaMoE layers no longer launch a separate EPLB mapping kernel, which saves 5–6 µs per layer. The replica choice is shared with the router through one Triton helper, so physical ids and load counts match `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` exactly.
- Async EPLB no longer adds a GPU→host sync to the decode loop. It also raises on every rank when the worker fails on any rank, instead of stalling.

## Validation

### GB300 NVL72

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-aarch64-dev-20261019`, which is main 49cb2bbf71 (2026-10-16) with this PR and #61395 copied over the installed `vllm` package. The PR code in the image predates the rebase and the last cleanup commit, which changes no runtime behavior.

Setup: decode only, DSpark with 5 draft tokens, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached). EPLB with one redundant expert per rank, `window_size` 1000, `step_interval` 3000, async. Throughput is the output rate from 120 to 240 s into the steady part of the decode pass, after EPLB's first rearrangement on steady traffic. The arms alternate on the same nodes, n=3 per arm.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | Target EPLB (tok/s) | Target + draft EPLB (tok/s) | Δ target (Welch t) | Δ both (Welch t) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 314.7k ± 1.1k | 349.8k ± 1.5k | 352.5k ± 1.0k | +11.1% (33) | +12.0% (43) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 586.0k ± 0.7k | 721.9k ± 3.2k | 732.7k ± 4.5k | +23.2% (72) | +25.0% (56) |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 710.6k ± 2.0k | 895.7k ± 0.9k | 897.1k ± 5.3k | +26.0% (147) | +26.2% (57) |

- Balancing the draft on top of the target adds +1.5% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank (t=3.4) and +0.8% at DEP16 (t=2.6). At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, +0.2% is not resolved (t=0.5).
- Balancedness (mean ÷ max rank load per step, 72 req/rank), off → on: target 0.50 → 0.95 at DEP16 and 0.35 → 0.94 at DEP32; draft 0.36 → 0.94 at DEP16 and 0.21 → 0.89 at DEP32.

Per-step GPU time, DEP32 with 128 req/rank (mean of four 3 s CUDA profiles per arm over one rearrangement cycle, all 32 ranks):

| | EPLB off | Target EPLB | Target + draft EPLB |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main-model MegaMoE | 14.65 ms | 7.62 ms | 7.63 ms |
| DSpark draft MegaMoE | 0.93 ms | 0.92 ms | 0.55 ms |
| All other kernels | 16.03 ms | 16.14 ms | 16.18 ms |
| Decode step | 31.70 ms | 24.80 ms | 24.47 ms |

GSM8K, same image and server flags, with EPLB rearranging during the eval: `num_redundant_experts` = DP, `window_size` 50, `step_interval` 150, so every pass runs five 40-layer rearrangements with requests in flight. A rearrangement takes 1.6–1.9 s at DEP32. 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, concurrency 64. Off and on alternate, with two server starts per arm and two passes per start.

| Config | EPLB off (4 passes) | `symm_mem`, target + draft (4 passes) | Δ, paired bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16 | 0.902 | 0.898 | −0.40 pp [−1.08, +0.27] |
| DEP32 | 0.903 | 0.905 | +0.21 pp [−0.45, +0.85] |

The number of questions whose answer differs between an EPLB pass and an off pass (66–95) is in the same range as between two off passes (71–92).

Tests after rebasing onto 5d35ce3934, one GB300 node with 4 GPUs, run from this branch's source inside the image above (the PR changes only Python files):

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py -k "eplb or capture"` (incl. `test_prepare_megamoe_eplb_maps_and_records_under_graph_replay`) | 5 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 34 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k "symm_mem or gloo or registers"` | 19 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py` | 14 passed |

### Earlier GB200 NVL72 runs

These runs show smaller EPLB gains than the GB300 runs above. Besides the hardware, they differ in build (nightly fe4df3df, 2026-10-12, before #56716 kept warmup out of the EPLB load stats) and in measurement window (the whole 16k-token pass, not a steady window after a rearrangement on steady traffic).

Hardware: GB200 NVL72, 4 GPUs per node.

Serving setup: DSpark with 5 draft tokens, MRV2, FULL CUDA graphs, async scheduling.

EPLB setup: `{"num_redundant_experts": <DP>, "window_size": 1000, "step_interval": 3000, "use_async": true, "communicator": "symm_mem"}`, i.e. one redundant expert per rank.

Workload: decode only, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached), 16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, and requests pinned evenly to DP ranks. Throughput is the output rate over the window in which every request is decoding.

Off and on arms ran interleaved (ABAB) on the same nodes. These runs used a branch of nightly fe4df3df (2026-10-12) with this change set and #61767, before the rebase and without the second commit.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | EPLB on (tok/s) | Δ | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 223.6k ± 2.0k (n=4) | 228.1k ± 4.2k (n=4) | +2.0% | 2.0 (not resolved) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 419.5k ± 1.3k (n=4) | 435.1k ± 5.8k (n=4) | +3.7% | 5.3 |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 500.7k ± 5.1k (n=3) | 539.4k ± 9.7k (n=3) | +7.7% | 6.1 |

- DEP16 step time, p50 of 2000-step windows at full batch, same build: 24.34 / 24.28 ms off vs 23.61 / 23.25 ms on.
- At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, one pass per arm is excluded. A host stall unrelated to EPLB cut that pass by 13–34%.

Per-step breakdown, DEP32 with 128 req/rank:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|---|---|
| Step time (CUDA events, unprofiled) | 38.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| GPU idle at the step boundary | 0.27 ms | 0.27 ms |
| Main-model MegaMoE (5 s CUDA profile) | 18.1 ms | 13.4 ms |
| All other kernels (same profile) | 21.5 ms | 21.2 ms |

The GPU never waits on the host, so the MegaMoE saving turns into step time. MegaMoE is about 40% of the step, which caps the end-to-end gain.

Microbenchmarks (GB200):

- **Fused EPLB staging**, one MoE layer, hidden 5120, top-k 6, 384 logical experts. Each arm is timed as a CUDA graph replay, median of 200. Outputs, ids and load counts match main bit for bit in every case.

  | Format | Tokens | Physical experts | main: `torch.where` + map kernel + staging | Fused | Saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MXFP8 | 432 | 400 | 9.4 µs | 4.2 µs | 5.1 µs |
  | MXFP8 | 768 | 416 | 11.0 µs | 4.7 µs | 6.3 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 432 | 400 | 49.5 µs | 44.0 µs | 5.5 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 768 | 416 | 49.1 µs | 43.8 µs | 5.3 µs |

  That is about 0.2 ms per decode step across 40 MoE layers.
- **Weight-migration bandwidth**, 2 nodes, one MegaMoE layer of 25 experts (470 MB):

  | Path | Bandwidth |
  |---|---|
  | `symm_mem` peer copies, intra- or cross-node over multi-node NVLink | ~808 GB/s (bulk), ~294 GB/s (100 per-tensor copies) |
  | NIXL, cross-node | ~88 GB/s (UCX picks RoCE, not multi-node NVLink) |
  | NIXL, cross-node, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp` | ~0.12 GB/s (TCP) |

- **MegaMoE kernel time under serving load**, DEP16 with 72 req/rank, layers 2–40: p50 per call drops 12.6–14.0% across three profiled runs (222→194 µs). Layer 1 is excluded because it absorbs cross-rank arrival skew.

Tests on one GB200 node with 4 GPUs, before the rebase onto 5d35ce3934. The GB300 section has the rerun after it.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` | 110 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k eplb` | 18 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` | 35 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU) |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k nixl`, NIXL installed | 7 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 6 passed, 28 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` | 13 passed, 7 passed |

GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (one node):
- Setup: 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, `num_redundant_experts=16`, `window_size=100`, `step_interval=300`. Every arm rearranged all 40 layers four times during the eval.
- Command: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`

| Arm | Accuracy (2 passes) | 40-layer rearrangement |
|---|---|---|
| EPLB off | 0.898, 0.901 | — |
| `symm_mem` | 0.897, 0.895 | 2.9–3.3 s |
| `symm_mem`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 0.889, 0.883 | 2.9–3.3 s, no sync error |
| `nixl` | 0.892, 0.886 | 2.7–3.2 s |

The EPLB-off and `nixl` arms ran on the commit before the final cleanup, which does not touch either path. Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate; `symm_mem`'s advantage is across nodes over multi-node NVLink.

## Details

**`symm_mem` backend**
- The receive buffer is one symmetric `uint8` buffer per EP group, set up with a single rendezvous and carved into per-tensor views. The backend checks the NVLink/MNNVL domain before allocating.
- Senders and receivers derive each receive row from the global placement with the same helper, so `add_recv` is a no-op. Push backends get every rank's rows through a new `recv_rows` argument to `set_transfer_context`. This argument is optional and other backends ignore it.
- Each `execute()` runs two CPU barriers. GPU spin barriers can deadlock against MegaMoE's cooperative launches.
- Rejected with elastic EP. The buffer lives outside the caching allocator, so sleep mode does not free it.

**Fused mapping**: `fused_moe/eplb_triton.py` holds the replica hash, map lookup and gated load count. The MXFP8/BF16 and NVFP4 staging kernels call it, and so does the router kernel. Routed-experts capture still sees logical ids.

**Async EPLB**
- Per-layer maps are committed with pinned non-blocking copies, and the worker thread fences `expert_buffer` reuse.
- Balancedness stats are read back non-blocking and logged in order once they land.
- `should_record_tensor` is rewritten only when its value flips.
- The per-step "all ranks ready" check runs over `cpu_all_reduce_`. A gloo ring all-reduce costs several ms per step at DP16/DP32.

**Also**
- `logical_to_physical_map` is sized to R+1 slots unless elastic EP is on.
- `compute_logical_maps` is vectorized.
- DeepSeek V4.1 decoder-replay padding and dummy rows are marked as padding, which complements #61643.

**CI**: the `symm_mem` execution tests need NVLink peers. They are added to the optional 8×H100 "Distributed DP + EP" job; the 4×L4 EPLB job skips them. The MegaMoE staging test needs SM100.

**Limitations**
- In mixed prefill/decode serving, per-rank prefill imbalance bounds the step. There, EPLB mostly lowers tail TTFT rather than raising throughput.
- Likely rebase overlap with #61786, #59168 and #41141. Offline placements without elastic EP (#41141) could exceed R+1 replicas.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Revamp CI/release deployment: collapse image tiers, unify build pipeline
commits.pr_body:
> **Companion PR:** vllm-project/ci-infra#820 (dual-mode pipeline generator — must merge together or with ci-infra first)

Currently on CI and deployment, we have:

- **Too many image tiers.** The old pipeline had six distinct image layers (base, ci_base, CI image, wheels, test, smoke), each driven by a separate script with its own cache keys and metadata handoffs. Adding or debugging any step required understanding all six.
- **CI and release were disconnected.** CI built images via `ci-bake-rocm.sh`; release rebuilt everything from scratch with its own scripts, Dockerfiles and keys, so what shipped was never built the way CI tested it.
- **Thousands of lines of bash nobody could operate.** `ci-bake-rocm.sh` alone was 2,737 lines. The ROCm build/deploy surface totalled ~12,000 lines of shell with no human able to read, modify or debug it under pressure.

In this PR, the purpose is to have:

**Content-keyed base images, one Dockerfile, one HCL, three readable scripts.**

1. **Stack** (`rocm/vllm-ci:stack-rocm-<Ks>`) — base OS + ROCm + PyTorch. Built only when `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` or `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py` changes (content key `Ks`). Pushed once; reused by every subsequent build.
2. **Runtime and test dependencies** (`runtime-rocm-<Kr>`, `test-deps-rocm-<Kr>`) — the runtime layers and the test-only dependencies on top. Content key `Kr` = `Ks` + the Dockerfile above the per-commit marker + pip requirement files + `rust-toolchain.toml` + `tests/vllm_test_utils` + the torchcodec script. Each is built once per key and reused by digest.
3. **Per-commit** (`rocm/vllm-ci:build-<build-id>`) — vLLM compiled on top of `test-deps`. A Python-only commit reuses everything below it and adds ~160 MB; a requirements bump rebuilds the runtime and test-deps; a csrc-only change rebuilds neither.

All images and caches use zstd layers (pulling needs Docker ≥ 23 or containerd ≥ 1.5).

**One shared `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`.** Named BuildKit contexts (`stack`, `runtime`, `test-deps`) are injected by the bake HCL, so the same Dockerfile builds on any stack without duplication.

**One static `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl`** replaces the dynamically generated `docker/ci-rocm.hcl`. All parameterisation is through HCL `variable` blocks from environment variables. Targets: stack (+ wheels), runtime, test-deps, the CI test image (+ smoke, compile cache, Python-only wheel), and the release (wheels, `vllm-openai`, smoke).

**`build.sh` (330 lines) replaces ~5,000 lines of shell scripts.** Modes: `keys`, `base`, `ci`, `release` (plus `release-base`, the release stack and runtime only). Each mode is a self-contained named section, readable end-to-end. Bake builds from a `git archive` export of `HEAD` (checked against `BUILDKITE_COMMIT`), so the content keys hash exactly the bytes that are built and file-mode drift on shared agents never busts the csrc cache. A registry error exits 75, which the steps retry.

**Trust.** ci-infra sets `ROCM_CI_REPO`: `rocm/vllm-ci` for non-PR builds of `vllm-project/vllm` main (AITER nightly excluded), else `rocm/vllm-dev` with `pr<N>-` (PRs) or `br-<branch>-<hash>-` (nightlies, branch builds) tags and caches. Trusted builds never read `rocm/vllm-dev`; release reads neither `rocm/vllm-ci` nor its cache.

**Release builds from the same Dockerfiles and keys as CI, in the existing release pipeline.** The ROCm group of `release-pipeline.yaml` runs on its own `cpu_queue_release` agents (no extra Buildkite pipeline, no AMD agents in the release cluster):
- `build.sh rocm release-base` (one at a time) builds the stack and runtime from source into ECR, once per content key. CI agents also run PR code, so release never takes images or build cache from `rocm/vllm-ci`; it uses only its own ECR cache;
- `build.sh rocm release` compiles csrc for all 9 GPU arches (gfx90a/942/950/1100/1101/1200/1201/1150/1151) and pushes `<ecr>:rocm-<commit>{,-wheels,-base}`. The csrc compile uses the shared S3 sccache (as the CUDA release does) and falls back to ccache without it;
- the release image is the same recipe and keys CI tests, not the same bytes: its csrc is the 9-arch compile, which no GPU step runs. Measured locally with fresh builders: 2 h 37 min cold, 4.5 min for the next release with an unchanged csrc.

**`publish.sh` (205 lines) handles release publishing.** It copies digests via `imagetools create` from ECR to the variant tags, Docker Hub (nightly) and S3 (wheels extracted from the `-wheels` image) — no Docker build, no layer transfer.

**ROCm 7.2 (apt) deprecated.** All `rocm_72` stack plumbing removed: `Dockerfile.rocm_72`, `Dockerfile.rocm_72_base`, `stack-rocm_72` bake target, `rocm72-check-amd` CI step, ROCm 7.2 release pipeline group and publish target. TheRock 10 (`rocm`) is the only supported stack.

**ci-infra is dual-mode.** The pipeline generator checks for `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh` in the vLLM checkout. Present → new pipeline renders. Absent (old checkouts, forks) → existing pipeline unchanged.

**Image pre-warming.** Base tags are content-keyed (`test-deps-rocm-<Kr>` contains the runtime and stack). A cluster cron job can pre-pull the newest one by digest, avoiding the simultaneous pull from every node on rare base rebuilds.

### What is preserved

- **Step key `image-build-amd`** — unchanged. Every AMD GPU test step continues to depend on it.
- **`SETUP_STEP_KEYS = {"ensure-ci-base-amd", "refresh-rocm-base-amd", "pre-commit"}`** (`ensure-ci-base-amd` kept for pre-revamp branch checkouts)
- **Smoke tests** — `test-smoke` and `openai-smoke` stages in `Dockerfile.rocm` (import checks during the build). The release has no GPU smoke step: release images are evaluated before they are pushed.
- **Process lifecycle** — `run-amd-test.sh` handles: `CONTAINER_TIMEOUT_S` wall-clock timeout (TERM, then KILL after 10 s), structured `[amd-ci-teardown]` lifecycle log events, exit-code propagation, DPX GPU partition lock, HF mount check, NFS xet redirect, GPU preflight, diagnostics bundle on failure.
- **Nightly tags** (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly*`, `base-nightly*`), S3 wheels and root index, perf-eval ECR image, credential boundaries.
- **AITER nightly** — with `AITER_NIGHTLY=1` the test image's AITER step installs the newest nightly wheel that fits the image's ROCm, torch and Python; `AITER_SPEC` pins one instead. The build checks the wheel with `find_spec` and `ldd` (importing aiter needs a GPU). ci-infra's old-layout path is unchanged.

### Net change

41 files, **+1,927 / −9,734** vs `origin/main`.

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` | 1,018 | 579 |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` | 476 | 424 |
| `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl` | 143 | 162 |
| `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh` | — | 330 (new) |
| `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/publish.sh` | — | 208 (new) |
| `tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` | — | 289 (new) |
| `docker/context/base-wheels/.keep` | — | new (gfx1250 COPY fix) |
| `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh` | 1,813 | 212 |
| `.buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml` | 88 | 43 |
| `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml` | 872 | 756 |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72`, `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72_base` | 1,497 | deleted |
| `docker/ci-rocm.hcl` | 411 | deleted |
| `.buildkite/scripts/ci-bake-rocm.sh` | 2,737 | deleted |
| ROCm `rocm/*.sh` scripts (7 files) | 1,097 | deleted |
| ROCm release scripts (3 files) | 298 | deleted |
| `requirements/build/rocm.txt` | 19 | deleted |

**ROCm build/deploy surface after this PR:** 1 Dockerfile (579 lines), 1 HCL (162 lines), 3 bash scripts (build 330, publish 208, run-amd-test 212 = 750 lines total).

### Follow-up infra tasks

- **`amd-cpu-pr` queue split** — run PR builds on separate hosts with their own Hub token, scoped to `rocm/vllm-dev`. One comment in `build.sh` marks the boundary.
- **Cluster pre-warm cron** — pre-pull the newest `rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-*` on CI nodes, pinned by digest.
- **Hub tag retention** — prune `pr<N>-*` / `build-*` tags in `rocm/vllm-dev`; define an expiry window for the content-keyed tags in `rocm/vllm-ci`.
- **First ROCm release after merge** — it builds the stack and runtime from source and compiles csrc cold unless the S3 sccache is warm (~2.5–3 h). Its build log should show the ECR cache export (`writing cache image manifest`); the next release then reuses it.
- **ci-infra base step** — add the `exit_status: 75` (registry error) automatic retry that `amd.yaml` has.
- **Stacked follow-ups** — csrc cache key and untrusted-namespace scoping; test-image parity (fast-exit plugin in the image, RDMA userspace, Ray compatibility trigger).
- **gfx1250 Dockerfiles** (`Dockerfile.rocm_gfx1250`, `Dockerfile.rocm_base_gfx1250`) — kept as-is, not wired into CI or release; needs owner sign-off before removal.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Gather the compressed KV once per KV-source group in prefill
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps compressed KV caches only on its kv-source layers (2, 8, 14 and 20 on V4.1-Flash); the other 34 compressed layers read their source's cache. The mega-attention prefill path still dequantized and gathered the whole compressed history in every compressed layer: 38 gathers per step for 4 distinct caches.

This PR gathers each source group's compressed history once per chunk:

- The gathered chunk sits in a retained span at the tail of the shared workspace (new `WorkspaceManager.get_retained`). Scratch requests come from the head, so they leave it alone.
- The span is keyed by source and chunk. A consumer reuses it when `get_retained` reports it intact under that key, and gathers again otherwise. Source layers always gather.
- The sparse indexer now requests its batch's K gather rows instead of the profiled bound. Before, it claimed the whole workspace and broke the span.
- No extra memory: the KV cache is unchanged (66.3 GiB on TP4).

## Test Plan

- TP4: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200, `vllm bench serve` with 128K prefixes plus 2K appends at concurrency 64. Base and PR ran side by side.
- PD: 2P1D on 16× B200 (Dynamo; 2× DEP4 prefill, DEP8 decode), aiperf AgentX trace at concurrency 2048, 30 min measured. Base and PR replay the same trace.

```

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Implements item 3b from the progress tracker in #54966 ("Test AITER backend and dispatch settings"): coverage for the `AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND` row ("Adaptive MXFP4 sorting"). Item 3a (#58393) added spawned-subprocess env-var-matrix coverage for the other three vars in that section (`AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING` / `AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING` / `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MOE_DISPATCH_POLICY`) but explicitly deferred `AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND` — that PR's description notes it "only fires on the MXFP4 path... not yet wired into `AiterExperts`", since at the time there was no way to drive `AiterExperts` through the MXFP4 W4A4 path in the modular-kernel test harness.

That blocker is now resolved: #60886 added MXFP4 W4A16/W4A4 oracle support and `MK_QUANT_CONFIGS` entries, and #60322 split `AiterExperts` into quant-specific subclasses including `AiterMxfp4Experts`. This PR adds the deferred coverage now that it's possible.

## What `AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND` does

It's a module-level global read once at `aiter` import time (`_MOE_SORT_BACKEND = os.environ.get("AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND", "auto")`), the same import-time-caching behavior as the vars #58393 already covers. It's only consulted when aiter's internal `output_aux` flag is set. aiter sets this unconditionally for a handful of MXFP4 a4w4 kernel families it ships — including the DeepSeek-V4.1 (DSV4) path this PR tests, and Kimi-K3's SiTU path (in fact the shape aiter's own adaptive/Opus crossover heuristic is tuned against). DSV4 is the only one of these the modular-kernel test harness can currently drive end-to-end — Kimi-K3's SiTU activation is real and default-enabled in production (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2="auto"`), but this test file currently marks it not-yet-implemented (`is_nyi_config()`) pending harness support for its weight-shuffle conversion path; that's tracked as a separate follow-up, out of scope here. No vLLM source change is required to exercise the DSV4 path this PR adds; this is purely a test-coverage gap.

Note on naming: despite being called "a4w4"/"W4A4" (aiter's own env var name, and the terminology #54966's table uses), DSV4 is reached through vLLM's **W4A16** modular-kernel quant key pair — activations aren't pre-quantized at that layer. AITER's DSV4 kernel quantizes them to 4-bit internally, which is where the "a4w4" name comes from.

## Why this matters

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` is a real production MoE path for DeepSeek-V4.1 on AMD, used when the specialized mono-decode kernel can't be used (for example expert-parallel or data-parallel deployments); it's validated against the model type and the installed AITER build version in `FusedMoEConfig.__post_init__`, not a debug flag. `adaptive` and `opus` are two distinct kernels in aiter rather than just a flag toggle: `adaptive` is a shape-restricted fast path, and `opus` is its fallback. Without this test, aiter silently falling back to `opus` for shapes `adaptive` is supposed to cover would regress performance without failing anything, which is exactly the kind of silent-fallback gap #54966 flagged as untested.

## Changes

- `modular_kernel_tools/common.py`: adds a `use_mxfp4_w4a4_dsv4` `Config` flag that opts a spawned worker into `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` and a `deepseek_v41` `hf_config.model_type` (required by `FusedMoEConfig.__post_init__`'s DSV4 gate), and converts weights via the production `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format(..., use_separated_a4w4=True)` path (DSV4's SEPARATED gate/up layout) instead of the gpt-oss INTERLEAVE converter used by the existing W4A16 test. It reuses `config.mxfp4_backend` (the same derived property the gpt-oss branch and production call sites already use) rather than a hardcoded backend constant. It also fixes a latent bug in `reference_moe_impl()`'s W4A16 oracle branch, which unconditionally assumed `SWIGLUOAI` activation — this fired incorrectly for the new DSV4 case too, which uses the default `SILU` activation, and surfaced immediately as a failure in the new test.
- `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: adds `test_aiter_moe_sort_backend_dispatch_env_matrix_mxfp4`, parametrized over `AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND` in `{opus, ck, adaptive, auto}`, using `AiterMxfp4Experts` on a real DeepSeek-V4.1-tuned MXMOE shape (`E=384, K=5120, N=640, topk=6, M=16`) confirmed against the installed `aiter` build's tuned kernel config CSV. The test skips (via `config.is_valid()`) rather than asserts on hardware support, since `AiterMxfp4Experts` requires gfx950 and this file currently also runs unconditionally on the MI300 (gfx942) CI lane (`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`); it will exercise the real dispatch path once #62907 lands gfx950 CI coverage for this file.

## Validation

Run on a gfx950 (MI355X) box, with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1` set before the test process starts (required by `require_aiter_moe`, or every case in this file skips):

Discovered while widening these tests' padded shapes; documenting following the same pattern as #60886/#62907. Both are AITER-side gaps worth a follow-up issue upstream -- worked around here via shape choice, not by catching the failure.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Deduplicate in-flight partial-tail loads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This is a small and focused bug fix that prevents duplicate asynchronous KV transfers for concurrent partial-tail hits.

When a partial-tail key is already being loaded to GPU, the scheduler now waits for the existing transfer instead of submitting the same load again.

## Claims

- Prevents duplicate GPU load jobs for concurrent requests sharing an in-flight partial-tail key.
- Preserves existing complete-chunk and synchronous-load behavior.

## Validation

The regression test uses real `Request` objects and `CPUOffloadingManager` state. The first request starts an asynchronous partial-tail load; a second request waits for that transfer and leaves the scheduler with one load job. Without the fix, the second request accepts the hit and creates a duplicate job.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and results</summary>

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k partial_tail_lookup_delays_duplicate_inflight_load
# 1 passed, 445 deselected

python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k 'partial_tail or sync_load'
# 20 passed, 426 deselected

python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
# 446 passed, 14 warnings

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
# All hooks passed, including check-test-tethering
```

</details>

## Details

The complete-chunk lookup already checks `_chunks_being_loaded`, but `_lookup_partial_tail()` previously accepted an offload-manager `HIT` without checking whether the same key was already loading to GPU. An offload manager can report the source chunk as ready while that earlier GPU load is still in flight, allowing a concurrent request to enqueue the same transfer. The fix applies the existing in-flight check to partial-tail keys; the existing retry path then waits for the transfer to finish.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Add chat template fallback for OpenVLA
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`openvla/openvla-7b` (supported since #42654) cannot be served through `/v1/chat/completions`: its tokenizer ships no chat template, so every request fails with HTTP 400. This registers a chat template fallback for `model_type="openvla"`, following the existing fallback mechanism from #17805. The template applies OpenVLA's training prompt format, so a chat request can carry just the instruction.

## Claims

- `vllm serve openvla/openvla-7b` now accepts OpenAI chat requests with an image + instruction (previously HTTP 400 for every request).
- A plain instruction (e.g. `Pick up the red block.`) is rendered as OpenVLA's training prompt, `In: What action should the robot take to pick up the red block?\nOut: `. Already formatted `In: ...\nOut:` prompts pass through unchanged apart from the trailing space.
- The final prompt always ends with token 29871, the token `predict_action()` appends when it is missing, so the prompt IDs match the upstream OpenVLA inference path.
- The prompt produced by the chat endpoint is token-for-token identical to the offline `LLM.generate({"prompt": ..., "multi_modal_data": ...})` path used for the HF parity check in #42654, and so are the generated action tokens.

## Validation

Same image, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=7`, on `d929755b7a` + this PR. The chat request sends only the raw instruction `Pick up the red block.`; the offline reference uses the model-card prompt `In: What action should the robot take to pick up the red block?\nOut: `:

| Path | Result | Prompt tokens | Action tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions`, before | HTTP 400: *"As of transformers v4.44, default chat template is no longer allowed, so you must provide a chat template if the tokenizer does not define one."* | – | – |
| `/v1/chat/completions`, this PR | HTTP 200 | 276 | `[31870, 31871, 31891, 31896, 31880, 31880, 31872]` |
| Offline `LLM.generate` (reference) | – | 276 | `[31870, 31871, 31891, 31896, 31880, 31880, 31872]` |

`prompt_token_ids` (requested with `return_token_ids: true`) are identical between the chat and offline paths: `[BOS] + 256 × image token + instruction tokens`, ending in 29871. All action tokens fall in OpenVLA's action-token range (31744–31999).

Template rendering was also checked against the `predict_action()` input (model-card prompt + 29871) for raw, capitalised/punctuated, and pre-formatted instructions (with and without the trailing space), each as plain-text and image+text content: all token IDs match. `test_openvla_chat_template` covers these cases, and `python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py -m openvla` runs and generates 7 action tokens.

## Details

**Root cause:** the OpenVLA HF repo has no `chat_template`, and `openvla` had no entry in `_MODEL_TYPE_TO_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FALLBACK`. Passing `--chat-template` works around it, but the fallback registry exists so that supported models work out of the box.

**Template design:**
- The last user message is treated as the instruction. It is trimmed, its trailing `.?!` is stripped, and it is lowercased (as in OpenVLA's training transform) before being wrapped as `In: What action should the robot take to {instruction}?\nOut: `. If the text already starts with `In:`, it is used as is.
- The prompt always ends in `Out: `. The trailing space tokenizes to 29871, which `predict_action()` appends when missing; without it the prompt would end in `:` (29901).
- The template deliberately emits **no** image placeholder: `OpenVLAMultiModalProcessor` inserts the image tokens right after BOS (`PromptInsertion`), and #42654 found that a text placeholder breaks HF parity. We confirmed this: a variant that renders a literal `<PAD>` (the image token id) per image leaves a stray token in the prompt (277 vs 276 tokens) and produces entirely different actions (`[31881, 31744, 31905, ...]`).
- System and assistant turns are ignored, since OpenVLA's action-prediction prompt has neither.

**Scope:** registry entry + template, a template unit test, and an `openvla` entry in `examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py` showing the prompt format. No model or processor changes. `setup.py` already packages `chat_templates/*.jinja`.

Fixes several problems in the PP sampled-token and draft broadcasts added in #50514:

- Remove a GPU<->CPU sync on non-last PP ranks. Received drafts were filtered with a boolean mask built via torch.as_tensor; the draft update now happens in the post_update kernel, reusing idx_mapping (which already marks excluded rows with -1).
- Avoid some unnecessary torch ops / gathers.
- Fix a race in broadcast_drafts: the gather from the shared req_states.draft_tokens buffer ran on the broadcast stream, so the main stream could overwrite those rows first. The gather now runs on the main stream.
- Skip the draft broadcast when no drafts were proposed this step (e.g. skip_drafts), and gate it on whether sampled tokens were broadcast instead of recomputing the mask.
- Size the sampled-token broadcast per step (1 column without drafts) instead of always padding to num_speculative_steps + 1.
- Move the EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state PP support check into set_eagle3_aux_hidden_state_layers.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fail loudly instead of no-op NCCL weight transfer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

An NCCL weight-transfer round can report success while moving zero bytes. `PyNcclCommunicator` disables itself (`disabled=True`) when the NCCL library won't load (e.g. on XPU) or when `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1`, and every collective then returns early. The workers keep their old weights, and an RL run trains against a frozen policy with nothing in any log.

This PR rejects a disabled communicator at rendezvous, in `stateless_init_process_group` and `uid_init_process_group` (trainer and worker, dense and sparse), on every platform. A weight-transfer group always has `world_size >= 2`, so on CUDA it only fires with `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1` or a missing libnccl, which is the same bug.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -k disabled_communicator
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/nccl_common.py tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py
```

## Test Result

- New test passes; it fails with the check removed.
- 2x Intel Arc Pro B70, RL trainer driving `/init_weight_transfer_engine` -> `/start_weight_update` -> `/update_weights`: before, every route returns 200 and nothing moves (`importance_sampling_ratio` 0, loss and `grad_norm` 0). After, the rendezvous raises on both ranks.

The code was co-developed with Claude Code.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][HiSparse] Fuse per-layer slot invalidation and shorten the all-resident resolver path
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cut HiSparse's per-layer decode overhead in GPU time and launches: fuse per-layer slot invalidation into one launch per step, mask CUDA-graph padding rows inside the resolver, and cheapen resolver arithmetic.

## Claims

- Slot invalidation: one launch per step instead of one per leader layer. On B200 with 78 index groups, each step drops from 374–759 µs to 3.5–162 µs.
- Resolver: 1.16×–3.69× faster per layer than main at every swept shape on B200, with bit-identical outputs.
- GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP8 B200, 16k/1k: mean TPOT −1.8% at c=16 and −0.5% at c=64.

## Validation

#### Microbenchmarks (B200, main vs PR kernels in one process, CUPTI device time)

Outputs are bit-identical between main and PR at every point.

**Slot invalidation per step** (78 = GLM-5.3 index groups):

| groups × tokens | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 61 × 64 | 367 µs (61 launches) | 9.9 µs (1) |
| 78 × 8 | 374 µs (78 launches) | 3.5 µs (1) |
| 78 × 64 | 634 µs | 13.0 µs |
| 78 × 256 | 759 µs | 59.1 µs |

**Resolver per layer** (top-k 2048, CUDA graph; main includes the padding `copy_` + `masked_fill_`):

| requests (rows/graph rows) | pages on host | main | PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 (64/64) | 0% | 9.2 µs | 4.6 µs | 2.00× |
| 64 (64/64) | 10% | 18.8 µs | 14.0 µs | 1.34× |
| 100 (100/128) | 0% | 15.3 µs | 4.8 µs | 3.19× |
| 64, MTP3 (256/256) | 0% | 20.0 µs | 11.4 µs | 1.76× |
| 100, MTP3 (400/512) | 0% | 48.8 µs | 13.2 µs | 3.69× |
| 128, MTP3 (512/512) | 100% | 54.7 µs | 47.2 µs | 1.16× |

PR is faster at all 36 swept points (1–128 requests, q=1/4, 0/10/100% host pages): 1.16×–3.69×.

#### End to end (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 8×B200, TP8, 16k in / 1k out)

Main and PR were run back to back on one node, interleaved, with 2 reps each and a server restart per point. Both have the same KV capacity (1.49M GPU + host tokens).

| concurrency | variant | output tok/s | mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | main | 802 / 809 | 15.84 / 15.67 |
| 16 | PR | 816 / 817 | 15.47 / 15.46 |
| 64 | main | 1265 / 1262 | 40.23 / 40.35 |
| 64 | PR | 1267 / 1270 | 40.12 / 40.02 |
| 64 | no HiSparse | 1327 | 38.27 |

Summary: −1.8% TPOT at c=16, −0.5% at c=64. That closes about 11% of HiSparse's remaining 2.0 ms TPOT gap to no-HiSparse at c=64; the rest is outside these kernels.

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len 18432 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}'
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts $((2*C)) --max-concurrency $C --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

Benchmarks compare main at `d0c20bb840` with this PR at `ab5afbdab6`. The later merge of main only routes the op calls through the HiSparse platform backend (#62592), and the unit tests were rerun on it.

**Tests**

- [x] `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py` → 103 passed on B200. New test: `test_hisparse_invalidation_covers_every_index_group`.
- [x] `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` → 5 passed on B200.
- [x] GLM-5.3-NVFP4 serve A/B on B200 (above).

## Details

Cut HiSparse's per-layer decode overhead on the GPU and in launches:

- **One slot-invalidation launch per step.** Today it's one eager launch per leader layer after the forward graph. The kernel now runs over (written tokens × index groups) using a cached device table of each group's `device_global_indices`. `HiSparseRuntime.invalidate_written_slots` is replaced by `HiSparseSlotInvalidator`.
- **Resolver masks CUDA-graph padding rows itself** from `num_valid_rows`, one block per padding row. This removes the per-layer `copy_` + `masked_fill_` and the `request_ids`/`row_indices` buffers. On main, one block masks the whole padding run serially, which dominates the launch on padded batches.
- **Cheaper resolver arithmetic.** Power-of-two block math uses shift/mask (compile-time for 64-row blocks), and the first row's top-k is loaded before the request lookups resolve.

- `HiSparseSlotInvalidator` caches one device table of `device_global_indices` addresses per leader set. It is built on first use, so steady-state steps do no H2D copy. All index groups must share one hot layout (checked).
- Remaining HiSparse TPOT overhead at c=64 (~1.8 ms vs no HiSparse) is outside these kernels.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these kernels.
